request.text:
{"body":"### Describe the bug

On Linux 7.1+, `crypto/aes.ko` (driver `aes-lib`) became its own module and also provides the `aes` alias. The `"aes"` in `boot.initrd.luks.cryptoModules` now resolves to it rather than `aesni_intel`, so `aesni_intel` is no longer copied into the initrd. dm-crypt opens the root device in stage 1, binds to generic `xts(ecb(aes-lib))`, and stays bound to it after `aesni_intel` loads in stage 2.

- 7.0 initrd: `arch/x86/crypto/aesni-intel.ko`
- 7.1 / 7.2 initrd: `crypto/aes.ko`, no `aesni-intel.ko`

### Impact

LUKS2 aes-xts root on PCIe 5 NVMe (`fio` 1M seq, QD8, direct):

| kernel | read | write |
|---|---|---|
| 7.0 | 12.4 GB/s | 13.4 GB/s |
| 7.1 | 5.1 GB/s | 4.7 GB/s |
| 7.1 + `boot.initrd.kernelModules = [ "aesni_intel" ]` | 12.4 GB/s | 13.4 GB/s |

`perf` shows `crypto_ecb_decrypt2 → aes_decrypt_aesni` with `kernel_fpu_begin/end` per 16-byte block.

### Check

```
grep -A6 'name.*: xts(aes)' /proc/crypto | grep -E 'driver|refcnt'
```

Affected: the accelerated driver (`xts-aes-vaes-avx512`, `xts-aes-aesni`, …) shows `refcnt : 1` (unused) and a generic `xts(...)` driver from the `xts` module holds the references.

### Suggested fix

Add the arch-specific accelerated modules to the `cryptoModules` default, e.g. `aesni_intel` on x86 (and the arm64 equivalents, `aes_ce_blk` / `aes_neon_bs`).

### Workaround

```nix
boot.initrd.kernelModules = [ "aesni_intel" ];
```

### System

NixOS 26.11 (unstable 2026-10-17), x86_64, linuxPackages 7.1.0 and 7.2.11.
"}

{"body":"<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built-in Copilot/Agent Host integration; VS Code 1.142.0 bundles the Copilot runtime
- VS Code Version: 1.142.0, commit `6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1`, x64
- OS Version: NixOS, Linux x64, glibc 2.44, Wayland/Hyprland
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Copilot CLI / Agent Host session startup and Copilot Chat
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Agent Host model selection; failure occurs before a model request is sent
- Logs:

[copilot-runtime-permissions.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33745991/copilot-runtime-permissions.txt)
[vscode-agenthost-runtime-failure.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33745992/vscode-agenthost-runtime-failure.log)

## Summary

The Copilot Agent Host cannot initialize on the NixOS-packaged VS Code 1.142.0 build because the bundled `copilot-runtime` executable lacks execute permission. The UI subsequently reports the downstream error:

```text
Cannot call write after a stream was destroyed
```

## Reproduction

1. Install/run the NixOS-packaged VS Code 1.142.0 build.
2. Open Copilot Chat and create or select a Copilot CLI/Agent Host session.
3. Observe that the session cannot initialize and sending a message fails.
4. Inspect the bundled runtime at:

   ```text
   /nix/store/wc2i861yv7lhj81050s19cfaakh091wm-vscode-1.142.0/lib/vscode/resources/app/node_modules.asar.unpacked/@github/copilot-sdk-linux-x64/prebuilds/linux-x64/copilot-runtime
   ```

5. Check its permissions and attempt to execute it.

## Actual behavior

The runtime is installed as mode `0444`:

```text
-r--r--r-- root root ... copilot-runtime
```

It is a valid dynamically linked x86-64 ELF executable, and its dynamic dependencies resolve, but the kernel refuses to execute it:

```text
$ "$runtime" --help
zsh: permission denied: .../copilot-runtime
exit=126
```

A syscall trace confirms the immediate cause:

```text
execve(".../copilot-runtime", [..., "--help"], ...) = -1 EACCES (Permission denied)
```

`ldd` also reports:

```text
ldd: warning: you do not have execution permission for ".../copilot-runtime"
```

The Agent Host log shows the resulting failure chain:

```text
[Copilot] Starting CopilotClient...
[Copilot] Using bundled runtime path: .../copilot-runtime
[AgentService] provider initialization failed before Automations could refresh for copilotcli Cannot call write after a stream was destroyed
```

The same error then affects all dependent Agent Host operations:

```text
Request 'listSessions' failed Cannot call write after a stream was destroyed
Request 'resolveSessionConfig' failed Cannot call write after a stream was destroyed
Request 'createSession' failed Cannot call write after a stream was destroyed
Failed to refresh models Cannot call write after a stream was destroyed
```

## Expected behavior

The bundled Copilot runtime should retain executable permission in the Nix package, for example mode `0555`, so that Agent Host can launch it.

If the runtime cannot be launched, VS Code should report the underlying process-launch error rather than repeatedly writing to a destroyed JSON-RPC stream.

## Diagnostics and isolation

The runtime file exists and is a valid executable:

```text
ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, x86-64, dynamically linked
interpreter: /nix/store/.../glibc-2.44-57/lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2
```

`ldd` reports all required libraries, including `libc`, `libpthread`, and `libdl`; no dependencies are reported as missing.

The failure is independent of:

- Copilot authentication;
- GitHub network connectivity;
- model availability;
- VS Code settings;
- profiles and caches;
- the user-installed extension directory.

Authentication succeeds, but it occurs after the runtime launch has already failed. Normal non-Agent-Host Copilot functionality is not the affected path.

A related Nixpkgs report, [NixOS/nixpkgs#573021](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/573021), documents the same packaging defect and identifies loss of executable permissions during ASAR extraction as the likely cause. That issue is the appropriate place for the Nix derivation fix; this issue reports the resulting VS Code Agent Host failure and misleading error propagation.

template: copilot_bug_report.md"}

Request 'resolveSessionConfig' failed Cannot call write after a stream was destroyed
Request 'createSession' failed Cannot call write after a stream was destroyed
Failed to refresh models Cannot call write after a stream was destroyed
```

## Expected behavior

The bundled Copilot runtime should retain executable permission in the Nix package, for example mode `0555`, so that Agent Host can launch it.

If the runtime cannot be launched, VS Code should report the underlying process-launch error rather than repeatedly writing to a destroyed JSON-RPC stream.

## Diagnostics and isolation

The runtime file exists and is a valid executable:

```text
ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, x86-64, dynamically linked
interpreter: /nix/store/.../glibc-2.44-57/lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2
```

`ldd` reports all required libraries, including `libc`, `libpthread`, and `libdl`; no dependencies are reported as missing.

The failure is independent of:

- Copilot authentication;
- GitHub network connectivity;
- model availability;
- VS Code settings;
- profiles and caches;
- the user-installed extension directory.

Authentication succeeds, but it occurs after the runtime launch has already failed. Normal non-Agent-Host Copilot functionality is not the affected path.

A related Nixpkgs report, [NixOS/nixpkgs#573021](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/573021), documents the same packaging defect and identifies loss of executable permissions during ASAR extraction as the likely cause. That issue is the appropriate place for the Nix derivation fix; this issue reports the resulting VS Code Agent Host failure and misleading error propagation.

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No - Not tested

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Bundled package is 0.70.0; the active extension version in every affected window has not been verified.
- VS Code Version: 1.142.0 stable, commit `6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1`
- OS Version: Windows 11 Pro, build 26300. Remote-SSH host: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS x86_64, kernel `7.0.0-38-generic`.
- Feature: The separate agent window connected to a Linux host over SSH, rather than only the ordinary editor chat sidebar.
- Selected model: Not verified for the failing query.
- Logs: Sanitized crash excerpts, heap-analysis results, and request-trace findings are in the follow-up comment. Private heap snapshots are available through an appropriate non-public channel.

## Summary

Opening/continuing existing conversations in the remote agent window repeatedly causes the remote `--type=agentHost` process to exhaust its approximately 2 GiB V8 heap. Ordinary Remote-SSH connectivity continues to work.

In the affected state, creating a chat directly in the agent window can also remain on "Initializing" and prevent submission. Creating a chat in the normal editor sidebar and then opening/continuing it in the agent window reproduces the failure.

The repository contains large untracked binary trace files. A metadata-only trace confirmed eight file reads totaling approximately 342 MiB, all requested as base64, during conversation activation. The installed base64 encoder uses character-by-character string concatenation; an isolated synthetic test demonstrates substantial heap amplification.

## Steps to Reproduce

These reproduce the problem in the affected environment; a clean-profile/minimal-repository UI reproduction has not yet been established.

1. Connect to the Linux host over Remote-SSH and open the affected repository, which contains untracked `.pcapng`, `.qmdl`, `.pcap`, and `.sdl` files.
2. Open the separate agent window with existing conversation/diff state restored.
3. Open/continue a previous conversation. Alternatively, create a conversation in the ordinary editor chat sidebar, then open and continue it in the agent window.
4. The UI stops responding or does not return a response, and the remote agent host aborts with V8 heap out of memory.
5. Automatic reconnection/restoration can repeat the failure approximately every 20–25 seconds until the restart budget is exhausted.

Expected: conversations initialize and respond without exhausting the agent heap; large binary-file content handling should be bounded.

Actual: `JavaScript heap out of memory`, `SIGABRT`, and "Transport lost (reconnecting)".

## Isolation / limitations

- Rebooting the remote host did not prevent recurrence.
- Temporarily excluding only the two largest untracked packet captures did not prevent another OOM.
- The encoder amplification is independently reproducible with generated data; the exact frontend decision to request these binary contents is not yet isolated.
- Extensions-disabled, clean-profile, and Insiders tests have not been performed."}

{"body":" Type: Bug ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Open a file tracked by git that has at least 3 lines, e.g. ``` aaa bbb ccc ``` 2. Delete the first line (`aaa`) entirely so the file becomes `bbb` / `ccc`. 3. Look at the quick diff decoration in the gutter. ### Expected The red "deleted" marker is shown above line 1 (at the top edge of line 1), since the removed line was before it. ### Actual The marker is shown between line 1 and line 2, which looks as if a line was deleted between `bbb` and `ccc`. ### Analysis In `src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/quickDiffDecorator.ts`, a `ChangeType.Delete` decoration is placed on `change.modifiedStartLineNumber`, i.e. the line *before* the deletion, and `.dirty-diff-deleted:after` in `media/dirtydiffDecorator.css` draws the marker at the bottom edge of that line (`bottom: -4px`). When the first line is deleted, `modifiedStartLineNumber` is `0`. The range gets clamped to line 1, so the marker ends up at the bottom of line 1 instead of the top. A possible fix: when `modifiedStartLineNumber === 0`, decorate line 1 with a variant class that draws the marker at the top edge (e.g. `top: -4px`) instead of the bottom. {"body":"<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not yet established; one affected server is provided by Pylance.

Type: Bug

Multiple MCP servers are failing to initialize in VS Code. I suspect a VS Code/client issue, but have not isolated the root cause.

Environment:
- VS Code: 1.142.0 stable
- Commit: 6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1
- macOS: 27.0.1 (26A434)
- Architecture: arm64
- Pylance: 2026.4.1
- Errors appear in agenthost.log under the Copilot harness.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open a workspace with configured MCP servers, including the extension-provided Pylance MCP server.
2. Start a Copilot chat/request that initializes the servers.
3. Open the MCP server status.

Expected:
Available MCP servers initialize successfully.

Actual:
Multiple servers enter an error state. Pylance reports:

```text
This server reported an error

failed to initialize MCP client: transport failure during send initialize request: Client error: error sending request for url (http://localhost:55260/stream)
```

Relevant observations from logs on 2026-10-21:
- Pylance failed repeatedly with localhost:55260/stream; another session used localhost:57080/stream and also failed.
- A remote HTTPS MCP server failed with the same "transport failure during send initialize request" error.
- A Sequel Ace stdio shim initialized far enough to report that it could not reach its local HTTP backend at http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp ("fetch failed").
- REA and the built-in GitHub MCP server connected successfully in the same earlier session, so the logs do not show every server failing.
- When inspected later, nothing was listening on local port 55260. It is unclear whether this is a stale extension-provided endpoint, a server lifecycle problem, or a separate issue.

Troubleshooting:
- Reloading/restarting VS Code and restarting the affected MCP servers have already been tried; the problem persists.

Please advise which agent-host/MCP diagnostics would help determine whether VS Code is retaining stale extension-provided endpoints or failing to start/connect to HTTP MCP servers.

"}

{"body":"### Problem

On a machine whose root device enumerates faster than its keyboard — in practice any NVMe root with a USB-attached (including internal USB) keyboard — the LUKS passphrase prompt in a systemd initrd appears **before the keyboard can produce key events**. Keys pressed in that window are silently lost.

On this machine (MacBookAir6,2, internal Apple keyboard on xhci, NVMe root, `boot.initrd.systemd.enable = true`, no plymouth) the window is reproducibly ~830 ms, which is almost exactly the time it takes a human to see a prompt and press the first key. The practical result is that the first character of the passphrase is dropped on essentially every boot, the passphrase is rejected, and it has to be retyped. It feels like the keyboard needs "waking up".

Two consecutive boots, monotonic seconds, from `journalctl -b -o short-monotonic`:

```
boot A     boot B
2.254      2.342    fbcon: Taking over console          <- prompt visible from here
2.768      2.826    systemd-tty-ask-password-agent:
                    Starting password query on /dev/tty1   <- prompt PAINTED
3.353      3.412    usb 1-5: new full-speed USB device number 4 using xhci_hcd
3.501      3.569    input: Apple Internal Keyboard / Trackpad as .../input1
3.613      3.649    apple 0003:05AC:0291.0004: ... USB HID v1.10 Keyboard
                                                        <- keyboard USABLE
```

Dead window: 845 ms and 823 ms. Deterministic, not intermittent — the root device is PCIe NVMe and present by ~2.7 s, while the keyboard needs `xhci_pci`, then sequential hub port enumeration, then the HID driver to bind. The disk wins every time.

Not a termios flush: in systemd v260 `src/shared/ask-password-api.c`, `ask_password_tty()` has only `tcsetattr(..., TCSANOW, ...)` at lines 829 and 965 and no `tcflush`/`TCSAFLUSH`/`TCSADRAIN` at all, so nothing buffered is discarded. The keypress is lost because no input device exists yet to generate an event from it.

### Why file this here as well as upstream

I'm also reporting the underlying ordering gap to systemd, where I think the real fix belongs — the password agent should not paint an interactive prompt before input is possible, and udev already computes `ID_INPUT_KEYBOARD`. I'll link that issue here once it's filed.

But nixpkgs already owns initrd generation and the `boot.initrd.luks.*` surface, this is cheap to express here, and users currently have no supported way to fix it at all — the only remedy is hand-authoring a systemd unit plus a drop-in against a systemd-shipped unit, which is well past what a NixOS user should need to do to type their own passphrase. boot.initrd.systemd.services.wait-for-keyboard = {

        # last word covers key codes 0-63 -- the letters and digits. Lid

    while ! have_keyboard; do

};
```

The snippet above waits for any input device with letter keys, which is a large improvement over not waiting and is probably the right default. But it is not airtight, and I'd rather surface that than have it discovered later:

- **A YubiKey satisfies the test.** It registers as an HID keyboard with a full letter-key bitmap (`fffffffffffffffe` in the last word, identical to the real keyboard) and on this machine enumerated roughly **700 ms before** the internal keyboard. With one plugged in, the generic check is satisfied early and the fix accomplishes almost nothing. udev's `ID_INPUT_KEYBOARD` doesn't distinguish it either.
- **Touchpads can share the keyboard's USB IDs.** The `bcm5974` trackpad here reports the same vendor:product `05ac:0291` as the keyboard, so filtering on IDs alone is not enough — the bitmap test is what excludes it (last word `0`).

Suggestion for the option: accept `true` for the generic "any device with letter keys" behaviour, and optionally a list of `vendor:product` pairs for people who need it exact:

```nix
boot.initrd.luks.waitForKeyboard = {
  enable = true;
  timeout = 5;                      # seconds, then prompt anyway
  devices = [ "05ac:0291" ];        # optional; default = any device with letter keys
};
```

### Measured result

| | stock | with barrier | + `xhci_pci`/`usbhid`/`hid_apple` in `boot.initrd.kernelModules` |
|---|---|---|---|
| keyboard usable | 3.613 s | 3.408 s | 2.989 / 2.997 s |
| prompt painted | 2.768 s | 3.464 s | 3.054 / 3.070 s |
| **gap** | **−845 ms** (prompt first) | **+56 ms** | **+65 / +73 ms** (keyboard first) |
| logged wait | — | 1300 ms | 900 / 900 ms |

The gap flips sign, so the prompt now reliably follows the keyboard, and the first keystroke lands. Total boot time is unchanged — the boot was already blocked on a human typing.

Separately, moving the keyboard's probe chain from `availableKernelModules` (loaded on udev coldplug) into `boot.initrd.kernelModules` (force-loaded by `systemd-modules-load` at ~1.95 s) cut the measured wait from 1300 ms to 900 ms across two boots, reproducibly. `xhci_pci` is the one that matters, since the whole USB enumeration chain hangs off it. That's a pure latency win and not required for correctness, but it might be worth a note in the option's documentation.

### Environment

- NixOS unstable 26.05.20261008.7c8764b, systemd 260.5, kernel 6.12.112, x86_64
- MacBookAir6,2 — internal Apple keyboard `05ac:0291` on xhci, driver `hid-apple`
- LUKS2 root with passphrase keyslot, no TPM/FIDO2 enrolment
- `boot.initrd.systemd.enable = true`, `console.earlySetup = true`, no plymouth
- Console on simpledrm/fbcon during initrd (i915 loads much later in stage 2)
"}

boot A     boot B
2.254      2.342    fbcon: Taking over console          <- prompt visible from here
2.768      2.826    systemd-tty-ask-password-agent:
                    Starting password query on /dev/tty1   <- prompt PAINTED
3.353      3.412    usb 1-5: new full-speed USB device number 4 using xhci_hcd
3.501      3.569    input: Apple Internal Keyboard / Trackpad as .../input1
3.613      3.649    apple 0003:05AC:0291.0004: ... USB HID v1.10 Keyboard
                                                        <- keyboard USABLE
```

{"body":"## Environment

- VS Code 1.142.0, commit `6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1`
- Bundled Codex 0.157.0
- macOS, Apple Silicon
- Codex in VS Code's built-in Chat; GPT-6-Astra selected through ChatGPT

## Observed behavior

In a newly created chat, the UI showed the ChatGPT-backed model, but the first turn ran through `vscode-proxy` and Copilot's Responses endpoint. The follow-up switched to the native ChatGPT connection and failed with:

```text
400 invalid_encrypted_content
Encrypted content could not be decrypted or parsed.
```

This is not limited to reopening old conversations.

## Reproduced startup race

An isolated test using methods extracted from the installed VS Code build reproduces this sequence:

1. `_materialize()` captures the `vscode-proxy` model selection and starts creating a thread.
2. Before creation finishes, `_changeModel()` receives the `openai` selection.
3. It updates `session.model`, but skips marking the session for reload because `session.threadId` is still undefined.
4. `_materialize()` finishes using the previously captured provider and sets `needsResume` based only on connection identity.
5. The pre-turn launch check does not reconcile the provider mismatch.
6. On the next turn, `_changeModel()` detects the mismatch and requests a provider switch.

The resulting cross-provider history replay is consistent with the observed encryption failure.

## Verification

- Selecting the provider before startup completes correctly.
- Changing it during pending startup reproduces the mismatch.
- An in-memory provider recheck detects the mismatch.
- Direct empty-thread tests against bundled Codex correctly honor explicit provider selections.
- No installed application files were modified.

## Expected behavior

Before sending the first turn, the thread's actual provider must match the selected provider, including when selection changes during asynchronous startup.

## Current-source status

The same faulty startup logic is still present in [current main](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1d7375ae2acbc3562f3c7b19e04fd337249423e1/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/codex/codexAgent.ts).
"}

request.text:
{"body":"Remove the `install_extension` agent tool (`copilot_installExtension`, `#installExtension`) and the `install-vscode-extension` skill from the Local (Copilot Chat extension) harness, and call out the deprecation in the 1.144 release notes.

The tool was hidden only for users who set `github.copilot.chat.installExtensionSkill.enabled` to `true`; they got the `install-vscode-extension` skill instead. The setting is tagged as an experiment, but the experiment value never reached the `when` clauses that switch between the tool and the skill. Both go away; the agent recommends extensions instead of installing them.

## Usage in the last 5 versions

Window: 2026-09-06 → 2026-10-20 (raw-table retention limit), local sessions only (Agent Host / Copilot CLI sessions excluded). Source: core `languageModelToolInvoked` (`toolId == copilot_installExtension`), which includes the calls `run_notebook_cell` makes on its own.

| Version | % of local tool calls | % of local tool users |
|---|---|---|
| 1.139 stable | 0.0017% | 0.32% |
| 1.140 stable | 0.0012% | 0.23% |
| 1.141 stable | 0.0015% | 0.18% |
| 1.142 stable | 0.0015% | 0.17% |
| 1.143 stable¹ | 0% | 0% |
| 1.139 insiders | 0.0017% | 0.49% |
| 1.140 insiders | 0.0009% | 0.33% |
| 1.141 insiders | 0.0011% | 0.23% |
| 1.142 insiders | 0.0011% | 0.23% |
| 1.143 insiders | 0.0015% | 0.16% |

¹ 1.143 stable shipped on 2026-10-18, so it has only about 2 days of data.

Counting only the calls the model chose to make (Copilot Chat `toolInvoke`), usage on stable falls from 0.27% to 0.13% of local tool users between 1.139 and 1.142.

## Work items

- [x] **vscode**: remove the tool from `extensions/copilot` (#343120)
  - Delete `installExtensionTool.tsx`, the `ToolName` / `ContributedToolName` / category entries, the `package.json` tool contribution, the `vscode` tool set entry, and the `enable_other_tool_install_extension` tag on `newWorkspace`.
  - Remove the `github.copilot.chat.installExtensionSkill.enabled` setting and the `install-vscode-extension` skill.
  - The new-workspace prompt recommends extensions in `.vscode/extensions.json` instead of installing them.
  - `run_notebook_cell` no longer invokes the tool to install Jupyter. `ensureKernelSelected` (the `notebook.selectKernel` kernel picker) already offers to install the suggested extension, with the user's consent.
  - Update the agent prompt snapshots.
- [x] **vscode-embeddings** (microsoft/vscode-embeddings#141): remove `install_extension` from `src/tools/toolsList.ts` so the precomputed tool embeddings no longer include it. The command embeddings for `workbench.extensions.installExtension` stay, because it's a regular core command.
- [x] **vscode-docs** (`vnext`, microsoft/vscode-docs#10520): call out the removal in `release-notes/v1_144.md` under **Deprecated features and settings**.
- [ ] Check ExP for a `config.github.copilot.chat.installExtensionSkill.enabled` flight and end it if one exists. Code never read the setting through the experiment service, and the `package.json` `when` clauses only see the user's setting, so any such flight had no effect.

Follow-up: #343125 removes `run_vscode_command` (#343126, stacked on #343120).
"}

This follows #343118 (`install_extension`). With that tool and its replacement skill gone, built-in prompts rarely need this tool.

## Usage in the last 5 versions

Window: 2026-09-06 → 2026-10-20 (raw-table retention limit), local sessions only (Agent Host / Copilot CLI sessions excluded). Source: core `languageModelToolInvoked` (`toolId == copilot_runVscodeCommand`).

| Version | % of local tool calls | % of local tool users |
|---|---|---|
| 1.139 stable | 0.0115% | 1.40% |
| 1.140 stable | 0.0089% | 1.04% |
| 1.141 stable | 0.0100% | 0.92% |
| 1.142 stable | 0.0123% | 0.73% |
| 1.143 stable¹ | 0.0092% | 0.27% |
| 1.139 insiders | 0.0108% | 2.63% |
| 1.140 insiders | 0.0096% | 1.98% |
| 1.141 insiders | 0.0177% | 1.74% |
| 1.142 insiders | 0.0171% | 1.33% |

The tool's command ID and arguments aren't logged, so usage can't be broken down by command.

## Work items

- [ ] **vscode**: remove the tool from `extensions/copilot` (#343126, stacked on #343120)
  - Delete `vscodeCmdTool.tsx`, the `ToolName` / `ContributedToolName` / category entries, the `package.json` tool contribution, and the `vscode` tool set entry.
  - Remove the `@vscode` participant's `vscodeCmdToolUseInstructions` prompt section.
  - Delete the `get-search-view-results` skill, which only worked by running `search.action.getSearchResults` through this tool.
  - `project-setup-info-local` skill: create Python script and package projects directly instead of running `python-envs.createNewProjectFromTemplate`.
  - `troubleshoot` skill: ask the user to run **Developer: Chat Diagnostics** instead of running `github.copilot.debug.collectDiagnostics` through the tool.
  - Update the agent prompt snapshots.
- [ ] **vscode-embeddings** (microsoft/vscode-embeddings#142): remove `run_vscode_command` from `src/tools/toolsList.ts`
- [ ] **vscode-docs** (`vnext`, microsoft/vscode-docs#10521): call out the removal in `release-notes/v1_144.md`
"}

{"body":"<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

Copilot sessions track their work in two places the user can't see from the Agents window: the `plan.md` plan document, and the `todos` / `todo_deps` SQLite tables the agent writes with its `sql` tool. The agent host already reads both (`CopilotAgentSession.getSessionPlan` calls `rpc.plan.read()` and `rpc.plan.readSqlTodosWithDependencies()`), but the only consumer is Mission Control's `extensions/getPlan` relay method. Nothing in the window renders them.

The runtime won't provide this for us. It declares no canvases of its own and only routes `canvas.open` / `canvas.close` to whichever participant declared one; the SDK's `canvasProvider` option is there so a host can declare canvases on its control connection. That's how the Copilot app does its Plan canvas (github/copilot-cli#4250, github/copilot-cli#4841), and it has no todos view either; github/copilot-cli#1724 asks for one ("TODO list is internally managed by the agent, but not surfaced to the user"). On the data side, the SDK documents `readSqlTodosWithDependencies` as reading "todo rows AND dependency edges … for structured progress UI" and emits `session.todos_changed` as a signal to re-read.

## Proposal

Add a host-provided **Todos** canvas for local Copilot sessions, behind the existing `chat.canvases.enabled` preview setting:

- The agent host declares it on the SDK control connection with `canvasProvider: { id: 'vscode:agent-host' }` and `canvases: [createCanvas({ id: 'todos', ... })]`, both in `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.24-preview.0. No extension process, no SDK or protocol changes. The stable provider id means the runtime keeps the declaration across reconnects instead of re-keying it per connection.
- Opening it serves a page from a loopback HTTP server (the same `LoopbackProxyServer` base the BYOK proxy uses) at an unguessable per-session URL. The page lists todos grouped by status with their blocking dependencies, a progress summary, and the plan document. It re-reads on `session.todos_changed` / `session.plan_changed` over SSE.
- Canvas listings tag it with a new `host` provenance so it shows up under **+ › Canvas** in the Agents window; the agent can also open it with `open_canvas`. Closing the canvas or disposing the session ends the served page.

Nothing changes when canvases are disabled or for ephemeral sessions. After #342369 splits the gate, this stays on the `chat.canvases.enabled` (rendering) side, so it keeps working with Copilot extension processes turned off.

## Out of scope

- Theming is light/dark only. Like every canvas, the page runs in a `WebContentsView` and follows `prefers-color-scheme`, not VS Code theme tokens. A native editor pane would need a canvas kind without a URL, which is a protocol change.
- Auto-opening the canvas when the agent first writes a todo. It would change the layout unprompted, and the agent can already open it when it decides to."}

{"body":"**VS Code version:** 1.142.0 (Windows x64)
**Copilot runtime (Agent Host):** copilot-runtime 1.0.95
**Harness:** Copilot (new default in 1.142)
**OS:** Windows 11

### Summary

In Copilot harness sessions, MCP tool calls to a remote HTTP server are cancelled after ~180 s with `MCP error -32001: Request timed out`, even though the server entry in the **user `mcp.json`** sets `"timeout": 600000`.

The same server defined in **`~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`** with the same `timeout` works: the call runs for 309 s and completes. In a **Local** harness session, the same long call isn't cut off at 180 s either.

So the per-server `timeout` from VS Code's `mcp.json` doesn't seem to be forwarded to (or honored by) the Copilot harness, which falls back to its ~180 s default (see github/copilot-cli#4749).

### Steps to reproduce

1. In `%APPDATA%\Code\User\mcp.json`, define a remote HTTP MCP server whose tool takes 4â€“5 minutes to return:
   ```json
   {
     "servers": {
       "MyLongServer": {
         "type": "http",
         "url": "https://<remote-mcp-server>/mcp",
         "timeout": 600000
       }
     }
   }
   ```
2. Start a new chat using the **Copilot** harness (default in 1.142) and invoke the long-running tool.
3. Observe the tool call fail after ~181 s with: `MCP server 'MyLongServer': McpError: MCP error -32001: Request timed out`.
4. Now remove the entry from `mcp.json` and define the same server in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "MyLongServer": {
         "type": "http",
         "url": "https://<remote-mcp-server>/mcp",
         "tools": ["*"],
         "timeout": 600000
       }
     }
   }
   ```
5. Reload the window, start a new Copilot harness chat, invoke the same tool: it runs past 3 minutes and completes.

### Observed durations (same server, same tool)

| Where the server is defined | `timeout` | Harness | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| user `mcp.json` | 300000 | Copilot | Timed out at 181â€“188 s (many runs) |
| user `mcp.json` | 600000 | Copilot | Timed out at 181 s and 212 s |
| `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` | 600000 | Copilot | **Completed in 309 s** |
| user `mcp.json` | 300000 | Local | Completed normally after 4 min 47 s |

Runtime log for the failures: `[rust:rmcp::service] cancelled {"id":"N","reason":"request timeout"}` at ~180 s after the call started.

Also observed: when the same server name was defined in **both** `mcp.json` and `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, the call still timed out at ~180 s. The `mcp-config.json` timeout wasn't applied in that case.

### Expected behavior

- The `timeout` property of a server in VS Code's `mcp.json` should be forwarded to Copilot harness sessions, the same as `url`/`headers`, or
- if that's intentionally unsupported, it should be listed under "partially supported" in #332782 and in the MCP configuration docs, with a warning in the UI.

### Impact

Since 1.142 makes the Copilot harness the default, every user whose MCP servers are defined in `mcp.json` (including servers installed by extensions or internal catalogs that only write `mcp.json`) silently loses their configured timeout. Any tool call longer than ~3 minutes now fails, where it worked in the Local harness.

### Related

- #332782 (MCP migration to Copilot Agent Host harness; user `mcp.json` listed as partially supported)
- github/copilot-cli#4749 (MCP calls time out after 180 s)
"}

         "type": "http",
         "url": "https://<remote-mcp-server>/mcp",
         "timeout": 600000
       }
     }
   }
   ```
2. Start a new chat using the **Copilot** harness (default in 1.142) and invoke the long-running tool.

       "MyLongServer": {
         "type": "http",

         "timeout": 600000
       }
     }
   }
   ```

| Where the server is defined | `timeout` | Harness | Result |
|---|---|---|---|

| user `mcp.json` | 600000 | Copilot | Timed out at 181 s and 212 s |

### Impact

Since 1.142 makes the Copilot harness the default, every user whose MCP servers are defined in `mcp.json` (including servers installed by extensions or internal catalogs that only write `mcp.json`) silently loses their configured timeout. Any tool call longer than ~3 minutes now fails, where it worked in the Local harness.

  Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

  <!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the
  cause. -->
  <!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report
  Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
  - VS Code Version: 1.142.0 (commit 6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1), user setup
  - OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise 26H2 (build 26300.9711), Entra ID joined

  ### Summary

  When Remote Tunnel Access is turned on from the VS Code UI (not installed as a service), the editor passes an
  access token to the tunnel CLI only once, at tunnel start. The tunnel keeps working while the relay connection
  stays open. If the relay connection drops later (e.g. `websocket pong timed out`), the CLI reconnects using the
  original, now-expired access token and gets `401 Unauthorized` from the Dev Tunnels API on every retry,
  indefinitely. The editor is still running and still has a valid Microsoft session, but it never passes a new token
  to the CLI. The tunnel stays offline until the user turns Remote Tunnel Access off and on again on the host.

  Setup:
  - Tunnel started via Accounts menu → "Turn on Remote Tunnel Access" → "Only for this session" (no service)
  - Auth provider: Microsoft (Entra ID work account, tokens acquired via the Windows broker)
  - Client: VS Code desktop on another machine, connecting via Remote - Tunnels

  Steps to Reproduce:

  1. On the host, sign in with a Microsoft account and turn on Remote Tunnel Access from the Accounts menu, without installing the service.
  2. Connect from a client machine and confirm the tunnel works.
  3. Leave the host running for longer than the access token lifetime (~1–2 hours).
  4. Interrupt the host's network long enough for the relay websocket to time out (e.g. disable the network adapter
  for ~1 minute), then restore it.
  5. Open Output → Remote Tunnel Service on the host.

  **Expected:** after the network comes back, the tunnel reconnects. If its access token has expired, it gets a
  fresh one from the editor (whose auth provider can acquire one silently), or the editor restarts the tunnel with a
  new token.

  **Actual:** the tunnel retries every 2 minutes with the expired token and gets 401 on every attempt (220+ attempts
  over ~7 hours in my case). The editor's Microsoft session stays valid the whole time (`getSessions` keeps
  returning a session in the Microsoft Authentication log), but no new token reaches the CLI.

  ### Logs

  Remote Tunnel Service log (identifiers redacted):

  ```text
  # Tunnel started, token passed once
  [info] Session updated: <user> (microsoft) (service=false)
  [info] login Spawning: ...\bin\code-tunnel.exe tunnel user login --provider microsoft --log info
  [info] tunnel Spawning: ...\bin\code-tunnel.exe tunnel --accept-server-license-terms --log info --user-data-dir
  <dir> --delegate-to-editor --name <tunnel-name> --parent-process-id <pid> --no-sleep
  [info] __VSCODE_CLI_STATUS__{"type":"connected","tunnelName":"<tunnel-name>","tunnelId":"<tunnel-id>","isAttached"
  :false,...}

  # ~40 hours later: relay disconnect
  info [tunnels::connections::ws] websocket pong timed out, closing
  warn Tunnel exited unexpectedly but gracefully, reconnecting

  # Network still down
  warn Error refreshing access token, will retry: failed to lookup tunnel for host token: connection error: error
  sending request for url (https://<region>.rel.tunnels.api.visualstudio.com/...)

  # Network restored: 401 every 2 minutes, indefinitely
  warn Error refreshing access token, will retry: failed to lookup tunnel for host token: response error: HTTP
  status 401 Unauthorized from https://<region>.rel.tunnels.api.visualstudio.com/tunnels/<tunnel-id>?tokenScopes=hos
  t&api-version=2023-09-27-preview (request ID <id>):
  warn Error refreshing access token, will retry: failed to lookup tunnel for host token: response error: HTTP
  status 401 Unauthorized from ...
  ```

  There's only one `Session updated` / `tunnel user login` entry for the whole session. In the Microsoft
  Authentication log, the Dev Tunnels scope (`46da2f7e-b5ef-422a-88d4-2a7f9de6a0b2/.default`) is requested once at
  tunnel start and never again, even while the 401 loop runs.

  ### Notes

  - The CLI can't recover on its own here. It only holds the access token the editor gave it. Where Conditional
  Access requires a compliant/managed device, the CLI can't sign in interactively either: device code flow fails
  with `AADSTS530033`. In those environments the editor is the only component that can get a valid token, so the
  loop never ends without manual action.
  - The same 401 loop happens when the tunnel runs as a service and the editor that supplied the token is closed.
  - Possible fixes:
    - on a 401 for the host token, the CLI signals the editor (it already runs with `--delegate-to-editor` and a
  parent PID), and the editor re-acquires the Dev Tunnels token and re-runs `tunnel user login`; or
    - the editor refreshes the Dev Tunnels token before it expires and passes it to the running CLI; or
    - the editor watches the CLI status and restarts the tunnel with a fresh token after repeated auth failures.

  **Workaround:** turn Remote Tunnel Access off and on from the Accounts menu (or restart VS Code) on the host. This
  needs access to the host, which is often exactly what the tunnel is meant to avoid."}

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.142.0 (commit 6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1, user install). Also reproduced with 1.100 (portable zip) and VSCodium 1.140.6880
- OS Version: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 (x64), Korean locale, Intel Core i5-1235U, 16 GB RAM

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Launch Code.exe (normal launch, or `Start-Process Code.exe -PassThru -Wait`).
2. The process exits after about 8 seconds with exit code -1073741795 (0xC000001D). A window may flash briefly. No error dialog is shown.



**Description**

VS Code worked normally until 2026-10-19. Since 2026-10-20 it starts, may flash a window briefly, and then terminates about 8 seconds after launch. The exit code is always -1073741795 (0xC000001D, STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION). No error dialog is shown.

The same crash happens with VSCodium 1.140.6880 and with VS Code 1.100, so it does not look specific to one build.

**Evidence**

Event Viewer, Application Error 1000, VS Code 1.142.0: faulting module Code.exe, exception 0xc000001d, offset 0x0000000006042f33.
Event Viewer, Application Error 1000, VSCodium 1.140.6880: faulting module VSCodium.exe, exception 0xc000001d, offset 0x00000000060d2de3. The offset is identical across three separate runs.
Report.wer loaded-module list for the VSCodium crash contains only Windows system DLLs, the app’s own native modules, and IMGSF50Filter_x64.dll (MarkAny Image SAFER). I uninstalled the MarkAny e-PageSafer products and rebooted, and the crash was unchanged.
With --enable-logging=stderr --v=1, the last log line is FileURLLoader::Start: ...workbench.desktop.main.js, with no FATAL/CHECK message after it.
Start-Process ... -Wait then $p.ExitCode returns -1073741795 every time.

**What I already tried (no change in behavior)**

--disable-extensions, --disable-gpu, --no-sandbox, --js-flags=--jitless, --no-cached-data, and combinations of these. Each run exits in about 8.1 seconds with the same exit code.
Fresh --user-data-dir and --extensions-dir; renamed %APPDATA%\Code, %USERPROFILE%\.vscode, and %USERPROFILE%\.vscode-shared.
Clean reinstall of VS Code; older version (1.100); VSCodium; a new local Windows user account.
Minimal PATH; no ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE or NODE_OPTIONS set.
Windows Security real-time protection off; no entries for Code.exe in protection history, Code Integrity log, or Defender operational log; exploit protection system defaults unchanged.
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth and sfc /scannow (sfc reported repairing files; the crash persisted after reboot).
Disk health reports Healthy; memory and page file are sufficient.
Code.exe Authenticode signature is Valid and the file size is normal.

**Other apps**

Discord, Slack, Chrome, and the Claude desktop app run normally on the same machine. A separate Antigravity app (v2.24.0) also runs.

Expected behavior: VS Code opens a window and stays running.

Actual behavior: The process exits after about 8 seconds with 0xC000001D and no diagnostic output.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Launch Code.exe (normal launch, or `Start-Process Code.exe -PassThru -Wait`).
2. The process exits after about 8 seconds with exit code -1073741795 (0xC000001D). A window may flash briefly. No error dialog is shown.



**Description**

VS Code worked normally until 2026-10-19. Since 2026-10-20 it starts, may flash a window briefly, and then terminates about 8 seconds after launch. The exit code is always -1073741795 (0xC000001D, STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION). No error dialog is shown.

The same crash happens with VSCodium 1.140.6880 and with VS Code 1.100, so it does not look specific to one build.

Event Viewer, Application Error 1000, VS Code 1.142.0: faulting module Code.exe, exception 0xc000001d, offset 0x0000000006042f33.
Event Viewer, Application Error 1000, VSCodium 1.140.6880: faulting module VSCodium.exe, exception 0xc000001d, offset 0x00000000060d2de3. The offset is identical across three separate runs.

--disable-extensions, --disable-gpu, --no-sandbox, --js-flags=--jitless, --no-cached-data, and combinations of these. Each run exits in about 8.1 seconds with the same exit code.

Clean reinstall of VS Code; older version (1.100); VSCodium; a new local Windows user account.
Minimal PATH; no ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE or NODE_OPTIONS set.
Windows Security real-time protection off; no entries for Code.exe in protection history, Code Integrity log, or Defender operational log; exploit protection system defaults unchanged.
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth and sfc /scannow (sfc reported repairing files; the crash persisted after reboot).
Disk health reports Healthy; memory and page file are sufficient.
Code.exe Authenticode signature is Valid and the file size is normal.

Discord, Slack, Chrome, and the Claude desktop app run normally on the same machine. A separate Antigravity app (v2.24.0) also runs.

Expected behavior: VS Code opens a window and stays running.

Actual behavior: The process exits after about 8 seconds with 0xC000001D and no diagnostic output.

No system restore points exist, so I cannot roll back.
Crashpad dump files and WER reports are available and I can attach them."}

To be more clear: 

- The horizontal scroll bar does not show unless the max line width is greater than current view port width. With `editor.wordWrap` set to `bounded` or `on`, an editor with a normal file will never has a horizontal scroll bar. 
- But with `git.blame.editorDecoration.enabled` set to `true`, a virtual text of git blame will show after current line, so the total length of this line could be longer than the editor, and thus the horizontal scroll bar shows up. 
- But when the cursor is set to another shorter line (so the virtual text after the previous long line does not exist, and there is a new one after current short line, and it does not run out of the editor width), the horizontal scroll bar remains.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. create a git repo and some commits, ensure the git blame has a proper length
2. set `git.blame.editorDecoration.enabled` to `true`, `editor.wordWrap` to `bounded`
3. adjust editor to a proper size, like, by making two columns. now no horizontal scroll bar is shown.
4. click a long line (a wrapped line is the best choice). now the virtual text of git blame shows after it, and the horizontal scroll bar shows up, and shift+scroll works
5. click another short line (a empty line best, ensure that line length + git blame length < editor width). now the lengths of all lines are shorter than the editor width, but the horizontal scroll bar remains, and shift+scroll works
6. close and reopen the side panel with hotkey (for keep the cursor position). now the horizontal scroll bar is gone as expected
"}

{"body":"When an extension is installed both locally and on a remote, uninstalling one copy can leave `Uninstall` enabled for that removed copy. This is confusing because it looks as if the uninstall did not work. I have seen inconsistent uninstall behavior in a WSL window. Looking at the code points to a state calculation that lets the remaining installation make the removed installation appear `Installed`. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Connect to a remote, for example `WSL: Ubuntu`. 2. Have the same Marketplace extension installed both locally and remotely. Both installed models need their Marketplace metadata populated for the completed-uninstall case below. 3. Open its details page, then use the remote installed section's context menu to uninstall the remote copy. Leave the local copy installed. 4. Check the actions on the retained remote row and, if the details page represents the remote copy, its `Uninstall` button. 5. Repeat in the opposite direction: uninstall the local copy while leaving the remote copy installed. ### Expected behavior The removed copy should transition from `Uninstalling` to `Uninstalled`, and its uninstall action should become unavailable. The surviving copy should remain `Installed` and actionable. It is fine for a removed row to remain visible temporarily. It should not continue offering uninstall as if that installation still exists. ### Actual behavior indicated by the code - Removing the remote copy temporarily disables uninstall, then enables it again after completion because the local copy remains installed. - Removing the local copy can leave uninstall enabled even during removal, because the remote copy is checked first. - For an extension applied to all profiles, the stale action can be labelled `Uninstall (All Profiles)`. ### Relevant code These links are pinned to commit `0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41`. 1. [`ExtensionsWorkbenchService.getExtensionState`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsWorkbenchService.ts#L2008-L2027) checks the remote, web and local collections without restricting those lookups to `extension.server`. The initial `this.installing` check does respect the server, but the subsequent collection lookups do not. 2. [`Extensions.getExtensionState`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsWorkbenchService.ts#L964-L972) matches installed copies by Marketplace identity without checking the model's server. A removed remote model therefore matches the surviving local model. 3. [`onDidUninstallExtension`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsWorkbenchService.ts#L940-L948) removes the copy from the correct installed collection, but the state lookup above can still return `Installed`. 4. [`UninstallAction.update`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsActions.ts#L908-L937) uses that state to enable the action, including its `All Profiles` variant. An installed model with a known server should get its state from that server. Marketplace models without a server still need to be able to reflect installations across servers. ### Verification The state lookup, uninstall-event handling, container updates and action-update methods were executed in an isolated harness with synthetic local/remote models. It reproduced the stale enabled action in both removal directions, for ordinary and application-scoped installations. Restricting the state lookups to the model's server in memory corrected those cases. This was source-level verification, not a full VS Code UI test or a fresh end-to-end WSL reproduction. ### Related reports - #211446 and its original report #207724 describe overlapping local/remote uninstall symptoms. This report narrows the problem to the incorrect state and enabled actions after one installation is removed. - #194993 describes a repeated remote-uninstall action, but was closed for insufficient information. The expected scope of uninstall and the details page's choice of local/remote target are separate concerns. This report is about the state of the copy that was actually selected for removal. {"body":"When an extension is installed both locally and on a remote, uninstalling one copy can leave `Uninstall` enabled for that removed copy. This is confusing because it looks as if the uninstall did not work. I have seen inconsistent uninstall behavior in a WSL window. Looking at the code points to a state calculation that lets the remaining installation make the removed installation appear `Installed`. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Connect to a remote, for example `WSL: Ubuntu`. 2. Have the same Marketplace extension installed both locally and remotely. Both installed models need their Marketplace metadata populated for the completed-uninstall case below. 3. Open its details page, then use the remote installed section's context menu to uninstall the remote copy. Leave the local copy installed. 4. Check the actions on the retained remote row and, if the details page represents the remote copy, its `Uninstall` button. 5. Repeat in the opposite direction: uninstall the local copy while leaving the remote copy installed. ### Expected behavior The removed copy should transition from `Uninstalling` to `Uninstalled`, and its uninstall action should become unavailable. The surviving copy should remain `Installed` and actionable. It is fine for a removed row to remain visible temporarily. It should not continue offering uninstall as if that installation still exists. ### Actual behavior indicated by the code - Removing the remote copy temporarily disables uninstall, then enables it again after completion because the local copy remains installed. - Removing the local copy can leave uninstall enabled even during removal, because the remote copy is checked first. - For an extension applied to all profiles, the stale action can be labelled `Uninstall (All Profiles)`. ### Relevant code These links are pinned to commit `0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41`. 1. [`ExtensionsWorkbenchService.getExtensionState`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsWorkbenchService.ts#L2008-L2027) checks the remote, web and local collections without restricting those lookups to `extension.server`. The initial `this.installing` check does respect the server, but the subsequent collection lookups do not. 2. [`Extensions.getExtensionState`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsWorkbenchService.ts#L964-L972) matches installed copies by Marketplace identity without checking the model's server. A removed remote model therefore matches the surviving local model. 3. [`onDidUninstallExtension`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsWorkbenchService.ts#L940-L948) removes the copy from the correct installed collection, but the state lookup above can still return `Installed`. 4. [`UninstallAction.update`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsActions.ts#L908-L937) uses that state to enable the action, including its `All Profiles` variant. An installed model with a known server should get its state from that server. Marketplace models without a server still need to be able to reflect installations across servers. ### Verification The state lookup, uninstall-event handling, container updates and action-update methods were executed in an isolated harness with synthetic local/remote models. It reproduced the stale enabled action in both removal directions, for ordinary and application-scoped installations. Restricting the state lookups to the model's server in memory corrected those cases. This was source-level verification, not a full VS Code UI test or a fresh end-to-end WSL reproduction. ### Related reports - #211446 and its original report #207724 describe overlapping local/remote uninstall symptoms. This report narrows the problem to the incorrect state and enabled actions after one installation is removed. - #194993 describes a repeated remote-uninstall action, but was closed for insufficient information. The expected scope of uninstall and the details page's choice of local/remote target are separate concerns. This report is about the state of the copy that was actually selected for removal. {"body":"### Summary
A new regression in `layoutDurationMs` was detected across 5 chat scenarios: *text-only*, *tool-terminal*, *thinking-response*, *many-small-chunks*, and *tool-read-file*. The increases range from +26% to +45% compared to the established baseline. This is a clear, multi-scenario regression outside the normal run-to-run noise, and is not covered by any open tracking issue or recent Slack thread.

### Evidence
- **text-only**: 135.66ms ±5.18ms → 170.99ms ±2.48ms (+26.0%)
- **tool-terminal**: 194.23ms ±8.08ms → 251.13ms ±7.13ms (+29.3%)
- **thinking-response**: 163.4ms ±4.21ms → 220.16ms ±6.32ms (+34.7%)
- **many-small-chunks**: 145.22ms ±8.37ms → 211.07ms ±17.66ms (+45.3%)
- **tool-read-file**: 147.21ms ±9.61ms → 191.44ms ±7.92ms (+30.0%)

All p-values are 0, indicating high statistical significance. The baseline window (last 2 runs) shows no such regression; this is a new, abrupt step up.

#### Trend (last 3 runs):
- Baseline 2 (b10961b, 2026-09-22): no regressions
- Baseline 1 (906af18, 2026-09-24): no layoutDurationMs regressions in these scenarios
- Current: large, multi-scenario jump

#### Suspect commit(s):
The only commit in the window that plausibly affects chat rendering/layout is:
- [`903d0d0`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/903d0d0) — "chat: reuse text buffers for checkpoint replay" (dmitrivMS)
  - Touches: `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/chatEditingCheckpointTimelineImpl.ts`, `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatEditing/chatEditingCheckpointTimeline.test.ts`
  - Landed after the last baseline run, before this regression appeared.

### Suggested action
- Bisect and investigate `903d0d0` for possible causes of increased layout time in chat scenarios. If confirmed, consider reverting or optimizing the change.
- If not the cause, continue bisecting recent changes to chat rendering or layout logic.

_No open issue covers this regression; please triage and file as appropriate._"}

{"body":"<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not checked in a normal workbench window. The automated reproduction isolates the built-in implementation with controlled service failures.

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.143.0, affected build `087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41`. The relevant implementation is unchanged on main at `5170ebe909381b6990cd686dc47da9c854bc5946`.
- OS Version: Windows x64; reproduced with the Electron unit-test runner and fake timers.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. In `src/vs/sessions/contrib/github/test/browser/githubModels.test.ts`, instantiate `GitHubPullRequestModel` with the existing mock fetcher. Make both `getPullRequest` and `getReviews` consistently reject with `GitHubRequestError` of kind `authorization`/HTTP 403 or `notFound`/HTTP 404.
2. Call `await model.refresh({ priority: 'background' })`, then `model.startPolling()` with the default interval.
3. Advance the test clock by one hour plus one millisecond, leaving the polling reference alive and the account/resource unchanged.
4. Count both fetch operations and inspect whether the model has loaded a PR.

### Actual

For either persistent failure:

```text
PR metadata calls: 61
Review-list calls: 61
Loaded PR: false
```

That is **122 failed fetch operations for one inaccessible PR in a simulated hour**, including the initial refresh. Polling remains scheduled at the normal one-minute interval, with no failure backoff or access-recovery gate. Multiple distinct inaccessible PRs multiply this background traffic.

### Expected

Persistent missing-resource/access failures should trigger bounded retry/backoff or a recoverable suspended state, rather than indefinitely polling both endpoints at the successful-operation cadence.

Recovery should still be possible after an account/access change, a resource change, or an explicit user refresh. Preserve ordinary successful polling, shared model ownership, and cancellation.

### Cause and Impact

- [Each refresh requests PR metadata and reviews together](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/sessions/contrib/github/browser/models/githubPullRequestModel.ts#L148-L156).
- [Failures are caught and logged](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/sessions/contrib/github/browser/models/githubPullRequestModel.ts#L176-L182), so the refresh promise completes without conveying a persistent failure state to the poll scheduler.
- [The poll cycle schedules the next refresh unconditionally while retained](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/sessions/contrib/github/browser/models/githubPullRequestModel.ts#L139-L146), using the 60-second default interval.
- [The session polling contribution keeps unknown PRs eligible for polling](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/sessions/contrib/github/browser/github.contribution.ts#L263-L277): an unavailable PR is not recognized as a merged, inactive PR.

This generates repeated background failures and warning/error logs, wastes requests, and can make the PR and Reviews domain failure rates rise together.

### Validation and Scope

- Both controlled 403 and 404 cases reproduced the exact 61/61 counts with the real model scheduling logic.
- They were executed alongside the commit-enrichment reproduction using:

  ```powershell
  .\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\github\test\browser\githubModels.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\chat\test\browser\sessionArtifacts.test.ts --grep 'failure telemetry investigation:' --reporter spec
  ```

  Result: **4 characterization tests passed**. These confirm the undesirable behavior; they are not a fix. The temporary investigation tests are not on main.
- Read-only live GitHub probes returned 200 for an accessible PR and its review list, and 404 for a nonexistent PR and its review list. The 403 polling case was simulated rather than changing a live account's permissions.
- The traced polling loop also predates the typed-client migration; this is not evidence that domain telemetry introduced the failure behavior.
- This report establishes repeat amplification, not the exact missing-resource or permission cause behind individual production failures.

<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not checked in a normal workbench window. The automated reproduction isolates the built-in implementation with controlled service failures.

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.143.0, affected build `087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41`. The relevant implementation is unchanged on main at `5170ebe909381b6990cd686dc47da9c854bc5946`.
- OS Version: Windows x64; reproduced with the Electron unit-test runner and fake timers.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. In `src/vs/sessions/contrib/github/test/browser/githubModels.test.ts`, instantiate `GitHubPullRequestModel` with the existing mock fetcher. Make both `getPullRequest` and `getReviews` consistently reject with `GitHubRequestError` of kind `authorization`/HTTP 403 or `notFound`/HTTP 404.
2. Call `await model.refresh({ priority: 'background' })`, then `model.startPolling()` with the default interval.
3. Advance the test clock by one hour plus one millisecond, leaving the polling reference alive and the account/resource unchanged.
4. Count both fetch operations and inspect whether the model has loaded a PR.

### Actual

For either persistent failure:

```text
PR metadata calls: 61
Review-list calls: 61
Loaded PR: false
```

That is **122 failed fetch operations for one inaccessible PR in a simulated hour**, including the initial refresh. Polling remains scheduled at the normal one-minute interval, with no failure backoff or access-recovery gate. Multiple distinct inaccessible PRs multiply this background traffic.

### Expected

Persistent missing-resource/access failures should trigger bounded retry/backoff or a recoverable suspended state, rather than indefinitely polling both endpoints at the successful-operation cadence.

Recovery should still be possible after an account/access change, a resource change, or an explicit user refresh. Preserve ordinary successful polling, shared model ownership, and cancellation.

### Cause and Impact

- [Each refresh requests PR metadata and reviews together](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/sessions/contrib/github/browser/models/githubPullRequestModel.ts#L148-L156).
- [Failures are caught and logged](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/sessions/contrib/github/browser/models/githubPullRequestModel.ts#L176-L182), so the refresh promise completes without conveying a persistent failure state to the poll scheduler.
- [The poll cycle schedules the next refresh unconditionally while retained](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/sessions/contrib/github/browser/models/githubPullRequestModel.ts#L139-L146), using the 60-second default interval.
- [The session polling contribution keeps unknown PRs eligible for polling](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/sessions/contrib/github/browser/github.contribution.ts#L263-L277): an unavailable PR is not recognized as a merged, inactive PR.

This generates repeated background failures and warning/error logs, wastes requests, and can make the PR and Reviews domain failure rates rise together.

### Validation and Scope

- Both controlled 403 and 404 cases reproduced the exact 61/61 counts with the real model scheduling logic.
- They were executed alongside the commit-enrichment reproduction using:

  ```powershell
  .\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\github\test\browser\githubModels.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\chat\test\browser\sessionArtifacts.test.ts --grep 'failure telemetry investigation:' --reporter spec
  ```

  Result: **4 characterization tests passed**. These confirm the undesirable behavior; they are not a fix. The temporary investigation tests are not on main.
- Read-only live GitHub probes returned 200 for an accessible PR and its review list, and 404 for a nonexistent PR and its review list. The 403 polling case was simulated rather than changing a live account's permissions.
- The traced polling loop also predates the typed-client migration; this is not evidence that domain telemetry introduced the failure behavior.
- This report establishes repeat amplification, not the exact missing-resource or permission cause behind individual production failures.
"}

{"body":"When an extension's details page is already open, selecting its remaining installation after uninstalling the other copy can leave the page bound to the old installation. The tab is reused, but its actions still target the copy it was originally opened for. For example, after removing a remote copy, clicking the surviving local copy should let me manage that local installation. It should not require closing the details page first. ### Reproduction scenario 1. Connect to a remote such as `WSL: Ubuntu`, with the same extension installed locally and remotely. Choose one that prefers to run on the remote extension host. 2. Open the extension's details page in an editor tab so it represents the remote installation, and leave that tab open. Set `workbench.editor.useModal` to `off` if needed to use a tab. 3. Uninstall the remote copy through the remote installed section's context menu. Keep the local copy installed, and do not reload the window. 4. Click the remaining copy under `Local - Installed` to open its details in the same editor group. 5. Compare this with closing the details tab and opening the local copy again. The existing tab should refresh to represent the local installation at step 4. The code path below instead retains the remote input. Closing and reopening the tab creates an input for the remaining copy. ### Where the old installation is retained The references below are pinned to commit `0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41`. [`ExtensionsWorkbenchService.open`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsWorkbenchService.ts#L1693-L1702) creates a new `ExtensionsInput` for the requested installation. However, [`ExtensionsInput.matches`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/common/extensionsInput.ts#L47-L66) compares only the extension identifier. Local and remote inputs therefore match, even though they hold different installations. The [editor group deliberately reuses the existing matching input](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/editorGroupView.ts#L1258-L1276). [`EditorPanes.doSetInput`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/editorPanes.ts#L425-L446) then calls `setOptions` rather than `setInput` when the inputs match and `forceReload` is not set. The extension editor's [`setOptions`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionEditor.ts#L464-L484) does not replace the installation; even its conditional re-render uses the existing input. The extension-change notifications do not correct this either: [`ExtensionContainers.update`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/common/extensions.ts#L234-L244) avoids rebinding a container when an event belongs to the other server. Keeping one details tab per extension seems reasonable. The problem is retaining its old installation when the user explicitly opens the remaining copy. Correcting the installation-state calculation in #343155 would not by itself update this input. ### Earlier report and verification This appears to be the same underlying problem described in #131568, which was closed as `out-of-scope`. The [maintainer's diagnosis there](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/131568#issuecomment-905418649) explains that an already-open editor keeps holding the local extension after a remote installation is added, and that closing and reopening the editor is a workaround. The scenario above exercises the other direction, after removal. I am filing this again with the current code references and a more specific scenario. The input-reuse path has been traced in the source; this scenario has not yet been independently replayed end to end in a fresh WSL session. 2. In window A, open five folders as native tabs and arrange them in the order 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
3. Open two more folders in separate windows B (tab 6) and C (tab 7).
4. Run **Window > Merge All Windows**.

**Expected:** Window A keeps its tab order and the tabs from the smaller windows are appended at the end: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.

**Actual:** The existing tabs of window A get rearranged. The order I built up is lost, and after every merge I have to drag the tabs back into place.

**Why this matters:** I work with many project windows as native tabs and keep them in a fixed order. I merge windows regularly, so every merge means manual reordering.

**Possible fix:** As far as I can see, both the menu item and `workbench.action.mergeAllWindowTabs` just forward `mergeAllWindows:` to AppKit (`Menu.sendActionToFirstResponder('mergeAllWindows:')` in `src/vs/platform/native/electron-main/nativeHostMainService.ts`), so macOS decides the order. VS Code could do the merge itself instead: take the window group with the most tabs (or at least the focused window) as the target and attach the remaining windows in their current order with Electron's `BrowserWindow.addTabbedWindow()`, which inserts a window after a given tab. That would keep the existing order intact.
"}

{"body":"When an extension is installed both locally and in WSL, I cannot reliably tell which installation the details page's `Uninstall` button will remove. Opening the extension from `Local - Installed` can show the remote installation instead, while the button still just says `Uninstall`. This is particularly confusing because right-clicking that same local row and choosing `Uninstall` targets the local installation. These two ways of reaching what appears to be the same action can therefore remove different copies. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Connect to `WSL: Ubuntu` and have an extension installed both locally and remotely, with the remote copy active. Use an ordinary extension rather than a language pack. 2. Close any existing details page for that extension, so this does not depend on reusing an already-open page. 3. Click the extension under `Local - Installed` to open its details page. 4. Use `Uninstall` on the details page, then reload the window to check which installation was removed. The page can target the remote copy, leaving the local copy installed, despite being opened from the local row. The action does not identify this change of target. ### Expected behavior Opening a local or remote installed row should respect the installation selected. The details page should also make the scope of `Uninstall` clear before I click it, especially when both copies exist. For example, `Uninstall Locally` or `Uninstall from WSL: Ubuntu` would make the current action understandable. A dropdown could offer the other installed locations. If removing both copies is offered, that should be an explicit choice rather than an assumption behind a generic button. The `All Profiles` wording should also make clear which installation it applies to. There is a remote badge with an `Extension in …` hover, so the page is not entirely without an indication. However, it is easy to miss that opening a local row has changed the target, and neither the uninstall label nor its tooltip explains the scope. ### Relevant code The following references are pinned to commit `0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41`. [`ExtensionsList.openExtension`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsViewer.ts#L122-L134) replaces the clicked extension with the matching primary installation from `extensionsWorkbenchService.local`, without matching the clicked row's server. In contrast, the [context-menu path](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsViewer.ts#L137-L143) does check the server. That accounts for the difference between opening the row and right-clicking it. [`UninstallAction.update`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsActions.ts#L923-L925) sets the label to `Uninstall` or `Uninstall (All Profiles)`, and the tooltip to `Uninstall`. Neither includes the installation's server. The [remote badge](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsWidgets.ts#L507-L517) supplies the separate hover indication. The backend [routes ordinary uninstall to the selected installation's server](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0f940e29fcd0ea44385b4c327bf74d81bd2d0e41/src/vs/workbench/services/extensionManagement/common/extensionManagementService.ts#L224-L238). Language packs have a separate path that includes copies on other servers. The UI should communicate the actual scope rather than leave the user to infer it. ### Earlier reports I previously reported this in #211446, which was closed with `wont-fix`. I am asking for reconsideration with the current code references above. In the [original discussion](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/207724#issuecomment-2064612389), the maintainer acknowledged that opening an extension chooses the active copy and agreed that it should open the copy the user clicked. This report concerns the choice and visibility of the uninstall target. #343155 covers incorrect state after removal, and #343164 covers an already-open page retaining its previous installation. Fixing those would still leave the ambiguity described here.
