{"body":"**Title:** Agent Host BYOK Responses bridge pairs minted `rs_byok_*` reasoning IDs with upstream `encrypted_content`, causing 400 "item_id did not match" on replay

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.143.0 (2d0b7506a36c1d6db9a466440131a8e01eab2289)
- OS Version: Windows

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Configure a custom BYOK model that uses the OpenAI Responses API against a provider returning `reasoning.encrypted_content` (e.g. a ChatGPT/Codex-backed endpoint), with reasoning enabled.
2. Start an Agent Host (Copilot CLI) session with that model and run a turn that produces a reasoning item and tool calls.
3. Send a second turn so the history, including the reasoning item, is replayed.
4. The request fails with the error below, and every retry fails identically (5 retries, then `session.error`).

```
502 Request Failed: 400
{"error":{"message":"The encrypted content for item rs_byok_mvif6wem_6t could not be verified. Reason: Encrypted content item_id did not match the target item id.","code":"invalid_request_body"}}
```

**Expected:** a replayed reasoning item is either unchanged from what the provider issued (same ID and ciphertext), or sent without `encrypted_content`.

## Evidence (from the session log)

- The failing ID has the form `rs_byok_<base36 timestamp>_<base36 counter>`, produced only by `nextId()` in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/byokResponsesTranslation.ts`.
- The first stored assistant message containing `rs_byok_mvif6wem_6t` already holds it with a 6036-char `encrypted_content` (SHA-256 prefix `7784e5eb1c`), `reasoningBlocks.provider = "openai-responses"`. So the ID was already minted when the client first stored the item; it was not altered later.
- Three different `rs_byok_*` IDs appear in the session and all fail the same way. No genuine upstream `rs_…` ID appears in a failing pair.

## Suspected cause

`toResponsesOutputItem` keeps a reasoning item's ID only if it starts with `rs`, otherwise mints a new one while copying `encrypted_content` through unchanged:

```ts
case 'reasoning':
    return {
        id: item.id?.startsWith('rs') ? item.id : nextId('rs'),
        type: 'reasoning',
        status: 'completed',
        summary: ...,
        encrypted_content: item.encryptedContent ?? null,
    };
```

When the real upstream ID is missing or not `rs`-prefixed, the item leaves the bridge as a minted ID plus ciphertext bound to a different ID. On replay, `extractThinkingData` (`extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts`) forwards `id` and `encrypted_content` as-is because `rs_byok_` starts with `rs`, and the provider rejects the pair.

I have not confirmed what leaves the real ID empty or non-`rs` in my setup. The invariant violation (an ID paired with ciphertext it was not issued for) is clear either way.

## Proposed fix

In `toResponsesOutputItem`, never mint an ID for an item that has `encryptedContent`: preserve the original ID, or when none is valid set `encrypted_content` to `null`. A test in `byokResponsesTranslation.test.ts` can assert that no output item pairs an `rs_byok_*` ID with non-null `encrypted_content` unless the value is the `vscode-reasoning-metadata:` marker.

## Notes

- Downstream proxies are not the source: Archestra `platform-v1.4.0-rc.56` forwards reasoning items unchanged.
- The ciphertext is opaque and the log has no outbound request body, so the original ID binding is unverified.
- Same upstream error reported elsewhere: openai/codex#25290, router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI#6108.
"}

{"error":{"message":"The encrypted content for item rs_byok_mvif6wem_6t could not be verified. Reason: Encrypted content item_id did not match the target item id.","code":"invalid_request_body"}}
```

**Expected:** a replayed reasoning item is either unchanged from what the provider issued (same ID and ciphertext), or sent without `encrypted_content`.

## Evidence (from the session log)

- The failing ID has the form `rs_byok_<base36 timestamp>_<base36 counter>`, produced only by `nextId()` in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/byokResponsesTranslation.ts`.
- The first stored assistant message containing `rs_byok_mvif6wem_6t` already holds it with a 6036-char `encrypted_content` (SHA-256 prefix `7784e5eb1c`), `reasoningBlocks.provider = "openai-responses"`. So the ID was already minted when the client first stored the item; it was not altered later.
- Three different `rs_byok_*` IDs appear in the session and all fail the same way. No genuine upstream `rs_…` ID appears in a failing pair.

## Suspected cause

`toResponsesOutputItem` keeps a reasoning item's ID only if it starts with `rs`, otherwise mints a new one while copying `encrypted_content` through unchanged:

```ts
case 'reasoning':
    return {
        id: item.id?.startsWith('rs') ? item.id : nextId('rs'),
        type: 'reasoning',
        status: 'completed',
        summary: ...,
        encrypted_content: item.encryptedContent ?? null,
    };
```

When the real upstream ID is missing or not `rs`-prefixed, the item leaves the bridge as a minted ID plus ciphertext bound to a different ID. On replay, `extractThinkingData` (`extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts`) forwards `id` and `encrypted_content` as-is because `rs_byok_` starts with `rs`, and the provider rejects the pair.

I have not confirmed what leaves the real ID empty or non-`rs` in my setup. The invariant violation (an ID paired with ciphertext it was not issued for) is clear either way.

## Proposed fix

In `toResponsesOutputItem`, never mint an ID for an item that has `encryptedContent`: preserve the original ID, or when none is valid set `encrypted_content` to `null`. A test in `byokResponsesTranslation.test.ts` can assert that no output item pairs an `rs_byok_*` ID with non-null `encrypted_content` unless the value is the `vscode-reasoning-metadata:` marker.

## Notes

- Downstream proxies are not the source: Archestra `platform-v1.4.0-rc.56` forwards reasoning items unchanged.
- The ciphertext is opaque and the log has no outbound request body, so the original ID binding is unverified.
- Same upstream error reported elsewhere: openai/codex#25290, router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI#6108.
"}

{"body":"Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.143.0
- OS Version: Windows 11

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In VS Code Desktop, select **Accounts** > **Turn on Remote Tunnel Access...** > **Turn on for all sessions (install as a service)**.
2. Open the **Remote Tunnel Service** output log (`remoteTunnelService.log`).

### Actual Behavior

Service installation fails with exit code 2 and falls back to an in-session tunnel:

```text
[info] serviceInstall Spawning: ...\bin\code-tunnel.exe tunnel service install --accept-server-license-terms --log info --user-data-dir ...\AppData\Roaming\Code --name <tunnel-name>
[error] error: unexpected argument '--user-data-dir' found
[error]   tip: a similar argument exists: '--cli-data-dir'
[error] Usage: code-tunnel.exe tunnel service install --accept-server-license-terms --log <level> --cli-data-dir <CLI_DATA_DIR>
[info] serviceInstall exit: + 2
```

### Root Cause

[ this section comes from my copilot agent, and I have not verified that it is accurate - Matt ]

Introduced in  #330480 :

•  TunnelProcessCoordinator._installService()  passes  '--user-data-dir', this.environmentService.userDataPath  to  tunnel service install .
• In the Rust CLI ( cli/src/commands/args.rs ),  --user-data-dir  was added to  TunnelServeArgs  and  AgentHostArgs , but not  TunnelServiceInstallArgs .
• The unit test in  tunnelProcessCoordinator.test.ts  mocks  spawn  and asserts that  --user-data-dir  is passed to  tunnel service install .
"}

{"body":" Type: Bug Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes. Reproduces with no user-installed extensions (fresh --extensions-dir). Built-in extensions remained active, including Copilot Chat, which is required to invoke MCP tools, so I couldn't test with everything off. - VS Code Version: 1.144.0-insider, commit 5170ebe909381b6990cd686dc47da9c854bc5946 (arm64) - Also reproduced on Stable 1.142.0, commit 6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1 - OS Version: macOS 26.7.1 (25G241), arm64 - GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.72.2026102104 (built in) Reproduced in a fresh instance (`--user-data-dir` and `--extensions-dir` pointing at empty temp directories), with the server configured only in the workspace `.vscode/mcp.json`: { "servers": { "datadog": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp" } } } Datadog MCP is used here because it is publicly reachable (a Datadog account is needed to sign in). ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open a window with a single folder (`a`) containing the `mcp.json` above. 2. Start the `datadog` server and complete the OAuth sign-in. 3. In Copilot Chat (Agent mode), run a read-only call, e.g. "Only run the Datadog MCP search_datadog_monitors tool with status:alert. Reply if it succeeded or not." It succeeds. 4. File > Add Folder to Workspace and add a second folder (`b`). The logs show the extension host is replaced. 5. Repeat the same prompt. ## Expected The call succeeds, or VS Code re-creates the authentication provider and refreshes or re-prompts for sign-in. This does not look like ordinary token expiry: the failing call happens about one minute after the successful one (14:01:00 to 14:02:04 in the logs), right after the extension host is replaced (14:01:50), and Reload Window restores access without my having to sign in again. The authentication state should survive an extension host replacement. ## Actual The call fails: "MCP server could not be started: 401 status sending message to https://mcp.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp: {"errors":["Unauthorized"]}". Chat reports "It did not succeed (failed with a 401 Unauthorized error)." Developer: Reload Window fixes it. Video (redacted): https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/310b2168-9123-4703-9073-456e853b4d66 ## Logs (local time, 2026-10-21) Extension host log: 14:01:50.097 [info] Extension host terminating: received terminate message from renderer 14:01:50.638 [info] Extension host with pid 73460 started Renderer log: 14:01:50.325 [info] ChatSessionStore: Workspace transition from 4a4b8c1f... to 1b181f93... 14:02:04.959 [error] [LanguageModelToolsService#invokeTool] Error from tool mcp_datadog-mcp_search_datadog_monitors ... MCP server could not be started: 401 status sending message to https://mcp.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp ... MCP server log: 14:01:01.918 [info] Discovered 37 tools (before the folder add) 14:01:50.146 [warning] Extension host shut down, server will stop. 14:02:04.487 [info] Starting server datadog 14:02:04.490 [info] Starting server from LocalProcess extension host 14:02:04.885 [info] Discovered resource metadata at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1/mcp 14:02:04.954 [info] Discovered authorization server metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/v1/mcp 14:02:04.955 [warning] Error getting token from server metadata: Canceled: Canceled 14:02:04.956 [info] Connection state: Error 401 status sending message to https://mcp.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp: {"errors":["Unauthorized"]} After Reload Window (new host pid 74019 at 14:02:17): 14:02:36.346 [info] Starting server datadog 14:02:37.425 [info] Discovered 37 tools (no Canceled warning, no 401) ## Possible cause (from reading source, not confirmed at runtime) Read at commit 6d62b1d (Stable 1.142.0), not at the Insiders commit: - MainThreadAuthenticationProvider keeps the RPC proxy of the extension host that created it. - Disposing the host delegate in AuthenticationService does not unregister the providers that host registered. - getOrActivateProviderIdForServer() reuses the matching old provider. - Calls on a disposed RPC reject immediately with Canceled. - McpHTTPHandle._fetchWithAuthRetry() only takes its forceNewRegistration branch when an Authorization header already exists, so with no token it ends in a 401. I have not captured the provider's RPC state in a debugger. Related: #341484 (similar symptom, Agent Host path), #313493 (auth not reacquired after a network transition). The reproduction itself > was on Insiders 1.144.0-insider (5170ebe) in a fresh instance with `--user-data-dir` and > `--extensions-dir` pointing to empty temp directories, so no user-installed extensions > were involved. {"body":"- Copilot Chat Extension Version: bundled with VS Code 1.143.0
- VS Code Version: 1.143.0 (commit 2d0b7506a3), also reproduced on 1.142.0
- OS Version: Windows
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): agent mode
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GLM-5.3 (via an OpenAI-compatible chat provider endpoint; stream includes thinking parts)
- Logs: not attached - the analysis below is from the session transcript (chatSessions JSONL) and the shipped bundles

## Symptom

While a chat agent response streams, words are broken mid-word with a blank-line
gap in between, both on screen and in copied text:

```
Verif

ying the fix
```

```
settings

.json
```

Observed with agent-mode streaming (tool-use turns). The transcript data itself
is intact - the breakage is in how streamed chunks are appended to the chat model.

## Root cause

Stream providers may emit **empty thinking parts** (e.g.
`{ kind: 'thinking', value: '', metadata: { vscodeReasoningDone: true } }`)
between adjacent markdown text chunks. Three code paths interact badly with them:

### 1. `updateContent()` merge lookup (chatModel.ts)

When a new markdown part arrives, the merge logic looks at the **last** response
part and merges into it only if it is markdown. The lookup skips only a couple of
kinds (`textEditGroup`, subagent-related). Any *invisible* marker part sitting
between two text chunks - an empty thinking marker, a `progressMessage`,
`undoStop`, `treeData`, `codeblockUri`, `hook`, etc. - blocks the lookup, so every
chunk becomes a **separate markdown part**. Separate markdown parts render with a
paragraph gap -> words appear split mid-word.

### 2. responseParts -> ChatModel part converter (workbench)

The converter that turns provider `responseParts` into ChatModel parts **drops**
empty reasoning parts (`case 'reasoning': u.content && ...`), so two markdown
parts that were separated only by an empty thinking part end up **adjacent and
unmerged** - the visible split. There are two copies of this loop (history/turns
and live view).

### 3. Source of the empty markers (built-in Copilot extension)

The bundled `extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js` emits empty
`vscodeReasoningDone` thinking markers on every thinking->text transition. When a
text chunk follows running narration, the marker lands **between two text
chunks**. A second twin-generator only fires once per transition, but the same
guard (`l = true` regardless of whether the same event already carried text)
lets the marker slip in directly after visible text.

## Suggested fix (upstream)

1. In `updateContent()` merge lookups, skip **all invisible marker kinds**, not
   only `textEditGroup`/subagent - the same set that `partsToRepr` treats as
   invisible (`progressMessage`, `undoStop`, `treeData`, `codeblockUri`,
   `extensions`, `pullRequest`, `voiceProgress`, elicitation, `hook`,
   `multiDiffData`, `mcpServersStarting*`, `mcpAuthenticationRequired`,
   `questionCarousel`, `planReview`, `disabledClaudeHooks`,
   `autoModeResolution`, `workspaceEdit`, `externalEdit`) plus **empty thinking
   markers**.
2. In the two responseParts->ChatModel converter copies, merge an incoming
   `markdown` part into the previous `markdownContent` part when one is
   immediately adjacent (empty reasoning parts were already dropped before the
   push, so adjacency is enough; real thinking/tool parts stop the merge).
3. Do not emit the empty `vscodeReasoningDone` marker when the current event
   already carries text (`l = !f.text` style guard), and don't emit it from
   `applyDeltaToProgress` while transitioning inside a text stream.

WARNING: One dead end worth recording: merging chunks inside the **session-state
recorder** (`markdown()` append without push) is NOT safe - the batch-push
session format does not re-sync every part, so an append-without-push silently
drops text. Merge in the model/converter layer instead.

## Workaround (verified on 1.142.0 and 1.143.0)

Monkey-patch scripts that apply fixes 1-3 to the shipped bundles (idempotent,
backup + `node --check` + auto-rollback):
https://gist.github.com/Kenny856/64b81a541623676097261f63f49b9472

Anchors are minifier-name dependent (validated byte-identical on 1.142 and
1.143 builds); after a VS Code update the scripts may need new anchors - they
abort safely when an anchor is not found exactly once.

Related: #315643
"}

{"body":"<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you would like. -->
Voice Mode should have a consistent connected appearance, without switching visual states between listening and speaking or showing repetitive placeholder hints. GPT Live usage should remain discoverable without showing a notification on every connection.

## Requested Changes

- [ ] Always show the blue listening animation while Voice Mode is connected, including idle, processing, speaking, and muted states; clear it on disconnect and preserve ownership gating, audio reactivity, theming, high contrast, and reduced-motion support.
- [ ] Remove the purple speaking accent from voice controls and the floating voice widget so connected voice indicators stay blue.
- [ ] Remove the “Listening...” placeholder while preserving transcripts and useful mute/manual-talk hints.
- [ ] Remove barge-in placeholder hints and interruption wording from manual-talk hints, without changing interruption behavior.
- [ ] Show the GPT Live/OpenAI provider information notification only on the first successful GPT Live connection, remembering it across reconnects and restarts for the profile. Failed or cancelled startup must not consume the notice.
- [ ] Identify OpenAI GPT Live in the Voice Mode hover when the current connection uses it, across both segmented and standalone voice controls; retain the generic description for hosted voice.

The shared connection visuals and hint changes should apply to both hosted Voice Mode and GPT Live.

Implementation: #343315."}

{"body":"### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11)

### Package name

gitlab

### Upstream version

### Nixpkgs version

19.4.2

### Changelog

https://docs.gitlab.com/releases/patches/patch-release-gitlab-19-5-1-released/

### Additional context

[10.0 CVSS](https://docs.gitlab.com/releases/patches/patch-release-gitlab-19-5-1-released/#cve-2026-110264---integer-overflow-issue-in-regular-expression-compiler-impacts-gitlab-ceee) integer overflow issue affecting gitlab ce/ee version 19.4.2

### Notify maintainers

request.text:
{"body":"I prefer the Local editing experience because it provides Keep/Undo review controls before code changes are committed.

After recent updates, it was difficult to determine why Copilot was directly modifying and saving files without showing the familiar Accept/Reject or Keep/Undo workflow.

What I eventually discovered:

- Agent + Local provides the review experience I wanted.
- Agent Host applies edits directly.
- The distinction between these modes is not obvious.
- Agent + Local restores Keep/Undo controls, including individual and all-changes review.
- The UI now uses Keep and Close in some places, which is less clear than the historical Accept/Reject, Keep/Undo, or Keep/Discard terminology.

For PowerShell, infrastructure, shell, Perl, and other large script files, the review-first workflow is significantly safer than immediate file modification.

Suggestions:

- Make the Agent Host vs Local behavior difference clearer.
- Make the Keep/Undo review workflow easier to discover.
- Consider renaming "Close" to "Discard" or "Undo" when proposed edits are being rejected.
- Consider providing a clear indication in the UI whether edits will be applied immediately or held for review.
- Consider documenting which combinations of Agent, Ask, Local, and Agent Host provide review-before-acceptance versus direct-edit behavior.

I initially assumed the Keep/Undo workflow had been removed because Copilot was directly modifying and saving files. After investigation, I discovered that Agent + Local still provides the workflow I wanted. However, finding this required significant trial and error because the distinction between modes was not obvious.

As an example, I spent considerable time trying to determine why Copilot edits were being applied immediately. I eventually discovered that switching to Local restored the review workflow with per-change and all-changes Keep/Undo controls. This capability still exists, but it was not obvious where it had moved or how to re-enable it."}

{"body":"<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

## Background

We are moving agent-plugin browsing from the Extensions view (`@agentPlugins`) to Browse in Chat Customizations (#340346, with installed-only Extensions sections restored in #341159). In the Copilot harness, new plugin installations are delegated to the Copilot SDK.

Plugins previously installed through the old Extensions-view experience were installed by VS Code and recorded in `installed.json` under its agent-plugins directory (~/.vscode/agent-plugins/installed.json). VS Code still reads that inventory through `MarketplaceAgentPluginDiscovery` and forwards those plugins to Copilot as client customizations. They have not thereby become SDK-managed installations.

The marketplace migration added in #341593 (following #341301) registers sources from `chat.plugins.marketplaces` with Copilot. It does **not** migrate the installed plugins recorded in `installed.json`.

## Request

Provide an explicit migration path for existing VS Code-managed plugin installations to Copilot SDK-managed installations.

The flow should:

- Identify eligible installations from VS Code's `installed.json` and resolve their SDK-supported installation sources.
- Detect plugins already installed in Copilot and avoid duplicate installation.
- Install/adopt eligible plugins through the SDK, preserving applicable enablement decisions.
- Report unsupported sources and per-plugin failures, with safe retry behavior.
- Verify successful SDK ownership before stopping client forwarding for a migrated plugin, avoiding both missing and duplicate contributions.
- Define how old installation records and files are retained or cleaned up without breaking the Local harness or other consumers that still depend on VS Code-managed plugins.

Migration of marketplace registrations alone should not imply that installed plugins have been migrated. Keep the existing compatibility path for installations that have not successfully migrated.

{"body":"<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

## Background

We are moving agent-plugin browsing from the Extensions view (`@agentPlugins`) to Browse in Chat Customizations (#340346, with installed-only Extensions sections restored in #341159). In the Copilot harness, new plugin installations are delegated to the Copilot SDK.

Plugins previously installed through the old Extensions-view experience were installed by VS Code and recorded in `installed.json` under its agent-plugins directory (~/.vscode/agent-plugins/installed.json). VS Code still reads that inventory through `MarketplaceAgentPluginDiscovery` and forwards those plugins to Copilot as client customizations. They have not thereby become SDK-managed installations.

The marketplace migration added in #341593 (following #341301) registers sources from `chat.plugins.marketplaces` with Copilot. It does **not** migrate the installed plugins recorded in `installed.json`.

## Request

Provide an explicit migration path for existing VS Code-managed plugin installations to Copilot SDK-managed installations.

The flow should:

- Identify eligible installations from VS Code's `installed.json` and resolve their SDK-supported installation sources.
- Detect plugins already installed in Copilot and avoid duplicate installation.
- Install/adopt eligible plugins through the SDK, preserving applicable enablement decisions.
- Report unsupported sources and per-plugin failures, with safe retry behavior.
- Verify successful SDK ownership before stopping client forwarding for a migrated plugin, avoiding both missing and duplicate contributions.
- Define how old installation records and files are retained or cleaned up without breaking the Local harness or other consumers that still depend on VS Code-managed plugins.

Migration of marketplace registrations alone should not imply that installed plugins have been migrated. Keep the existing compatibility path for installations that have not successfully migrated.

## Relevant code

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/plugins/fileBackedInstalledPluginsStore.ts`
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/plugins/agentPluginServiceImpl.ts` — `MarketplaceAgentPluginDiscovery`
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostLocalCustomizations.ts` — `resolveCustomizationRefs`

{"body":"Opening an existing session in the Agents window that is not loaded yet takes ~2.5–5 s. About two thirds of that is spent waiting for Copilot Connector reconciliation, which restarts the session's Connector MCP servers and only returns after their **remote** MCP handshake has completed — none of which is needed to show the session.

**Version:** Insiders 1.144.0 (`5170ebe909381b6990cd686dc47da9c854bc5946`), macOS arm64, Copilot Connectors enabled (agent host `mcpConnectorsEnabled`), with one Connector configured (Slack).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have Copilot Connectors enabled with at least one Connector (e.g. Slack).
2. In the Agents window, click a session that has not been opened since the agent host started (or was evicted).
3. Observe the session takes several seconds to appear.

## Evidence

### One click, end to end

Agent Host Protocol transport log (`logs/<ts>/ahp/*.jsonl`) and `agenthost.log` for a single click (local time):

| Time | Step |
|---|---|
| 22:22:45.996 | client → `subscribe ahp-session:/9cdc…` |
| 46.035 → 46.212 | SDK `resumeSession` (177 ms) |
| 46.212 → 46.729 | agent catalog, script safety, sandbox `options.update` (~0.5 s) |
| **46.729 → 48.537** | **`reconcileCopilotConnectors` (1.81 s)** |
| 48.618 | `Restored session … with 5 turns` |
| 48.635 | subscribe result returned to the client (2.64 s after the click) |

The renderer was idle during this time (no long animation frames); it was waiting on the agent host.

### The wait is the Connector MCP server's remote handshake

The Copilot runtime log (`~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`) shows the reconcile RPC returns right after the session's Connector MCP server (`Slack MCP`) finishes `initialize`:

```
20:22:48.536Z [INFO] [rust:rmcp::service] Service initialized as client {… server_info: Some(Implementation { name: "Slack MCP", … }) …}
22:22:48.537 [info] [Copilot:2776f018-…] Reconciled 1 connector MCP server(s) through the Copilot runtime
```

This holds for **every** launch in that agent host process: across 35 session launches (create and resume), the `Reconciled …` log follows a `Slack MCP` `initialize` by 0–9 ms (two outliers at ~140 ms under 12 concurrent launches).

| | min | median | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| Connector reconcile (sandbox applied → `Reconciled`) | 1.71 s | **2.08 s** | 3.44 s |
| Whole launch (`Preparing SDK session` → `Reconciled`) | 1.92 s | 3.13 s | 5.03 s |
| Share of launch spent in reconcile | | **67 %** | |

### Why it blocks

[`CopilotSessionLauncher._finalizeSession`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionLauncher.ts) awaits [`reconcileCopilotConnectors`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotConnectors.ts) before returning the SDK session. That is `connectors.getCapabilities` → `connectors.getAccount` → `connectors.reconcile({ refreshCatalog: true })`, and the last call resolves only after the runtime has (re)started the Connector-owned MCP servers. The session cannot be restored — and the subscribe cannot answer — until then.

Nothing about displaying a session depends on Connector state. What does depend on it:

- a turn's tool set (the Connector servers must be bound to the session account before the model can use them),
- MCP server start/stop,
- Connector refreshes (`CopilotAgentSession.refreshConnectors`),
- deciding whether a pending MCP auth request belongs to a Connector (a Connector-owned server must never receive a client-provided MCP token).

## Proposal

Start the launch-time reconcile at the same point but don't await it in the launcher; hand it to the `CopilotAgentSession`, which publishes its result (Connector ownership, MCP inventory, `tools/list_changed`) when it settles and makes the four dependents above wait for it. Opening a session then costs ~0.8 s instead of ~2.6 s in the trace above, and the reconcile usually finishes in the background before the user sends anything. If they send immediately, the first turn waits for the remainder, which is exactly what every open pays today.
"}

{"body":"<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

## Problem

VS Code currently reads `~/.copilot/config.json` on the client to discover Copilot CLI/SDK-managed plugin installations. `CopilotCliInstalledPluginsStore` reads the installed-plugin records and resolves their cache paths, and `CopilotCliAgentPluginDiscovery` parses those directories into the shared workbench plugin inventory.

Those plugins can subsequently be forwarded back to Copilot as client customizations. Copilot already owns these installations and should be responsible for detecting them and reporting their contents. The client should not depend on Copilot's private configuration-file schema or installed-plugin cache layout.

## Requested change

Make Copilot/the agent host authoritative for SDK-managed plugin discovery and content publication:

- Stop reading and watching `~/.copilot/config.json` for plugin discovery on the VS Code client.
- Remove the corresponding client dependency on SDK-managed plugin cache paths and filesystem parsing.
- Have Copilot detect its installed plugins and publish their contents through the agent-host customization model, including skills, agents, commands, instructions, hooks, and MCP server definitions as applicable.
- Include plugins that contribute only hooks or MCP servers, not just plugins identifiable through SDK-reported prompt files.
- Keep the customization UI, enablement, install/uninstall refresh, and content navigation working from provider-published inventory and content.
- Do not forward SDK-managed installations back to Copilot as client plugins.
- Respect the selected host's inventory for remote sessions rather than assuming the client's local Copilot installation inventory is applicable.

Keep client forwarding for genuinely client-provided plugins: extension-contributed plugins, explicit `chat.pluginLocations`, and existing VS Code-managed installations until their separate migration is completed.

## Related work

- #343334 tracks migration of VS Code-managed installations from `installed.json` to Copilot SDK ownership. This request concerns plugins that are already SDK-managed.
- #341301 established provider-owned Copilot marketplace management.

## Relevant code

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/plugins/agentPluginServiceImpl.ts` — `CopilotCliInstalledPluginsStore` and `CopilotCliAgentPluginDiscovery`
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostLocalCustomizations.ts` — `resolveCustomizationRefs`
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/sessionCustomizationDiscovery.ts` — existing host projection of SDK-native plugins; currently notes that hooks-only and MCP-only plugins lack an SDK-reported file anchor"}

{"body":"Follow-up from #342852, which turned the product build (ADO def 111) red on `Unit Tests (Electron)` on all 3 OSes. Examples: main CI [487717](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=487717) and [487749](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=487749). Details are in [this comment](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/342852#issuecomment-6326264774) and microsoft/vscode-engineering#4294.

## What's wrong

Product builds use the Microsoft-built Electron that we ship. The distro `product.json` sets `electronArtifactFeed: vscode-electron-prebuilt`, and `build/lib/electron.ts` downloads Electron from that feed. PR CI and local dev use the public Electron release.

On the feed Electron, a VP8 WebM doesn't decode in a `<video>` element on Linux, macOS or Windows. Even a clip recorded by `MediaRecorder` in the same process can't be played back. On public Electron the same tests pass, including with `--build`.

**This likely means WebM import, and possibly recording playback, doesn't work in Insiders.** WebM recording predates #342852 (`recordingService.ts`, `nativeRecordingService.ts`, and the `<video>` in `issueReporterEditorPane.ts`), so the playback part may be a pre-existing limitation of the feed Electron that these new tests exposed, separate from the new import path.

I couldn't download the feed Electron on my machine, so the shipped-runtime part is inferred from CI failing identically on all 3 OSes. It isn't reproduced locally.

## Tests skipped until this is fixed

To keep official Insiders building, these 4 tests are skipped with a link to this issue. That change is a temporary fix PR; I'll link it here.
- `Issue reporter media decoding › decodes real webm or explicitly rejects an unsupported container, with complete cleanup`
- `Issue reporter media decoding › does not invent a duration for a playable WebM recording without duration metadata`
- `Issue reporter media import lifecycle › does not present Chromium's last-frame estimate as the duration of an imported WebM`
- `NativeRecordingService › encodes and decodes playable video/webm without OS capture`

## Asks for @Giuspepe

1. **Check whether recording playback already fails in current Insiders.** If it does, the problem predates #342852 and lives in the feed Electron.
2. Decide the product behavior when WebM can't be decoded on the shipped runtime. Options include a different container or codec, a clear error, or getting the feed Electron fixed.
3. Run the media tests on the feed Electron, for example through a def 111 run or `scripts/test.sh` with the feed build, before un-skipping them.

> Co-authored with Copilot
"}

{"body":"<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

## Problem

An expected authentication or consent flow opens a URL on `https://logic-apis-centralus.consent.azure-apim.net`. Because this exact Microsoft-controlled endpoint is not in the product's `linkProtectionTrustedDomains`, VS Code displays its external-link confirmation before handing the request to the browser:

![External website confirmation shown for the Logic Apps consent endpoint](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3828151e-88d3-4244-8ae8-435215aee2f2)

This adds an unexpected security prompt in the middle of an intentional sign-in flow. The user must inspect a long, truncated URL and choose **Open** before reaching the browser-hosted login or consent experience.

## Proposed experience

Add the exact origin below to the product-level trusted-domain list for Stable, Insiders, and Exploration:

`https://logic-apis-centralus.consent.azure-apim.net`

After the change, an intentional navigation to this origin should open directly in the user's default browser. Browser authentication, consent, and security checks remain unchanged; only VS Code's redundant external-link confirmation is skipped.

## Rationale and scope

- The endpoint is part of the expected Logic Apps authentication/consent flow.
- Removing the intermediate confirmation makes the flow feel continuous and avoids asking users to make a security decision based on a truncated infrastructure URL.
- The allowlist entry should be restricted to the exact HTTPS hostname. Do not add `*.azure-apim.net` or another broader wildcard.
- Trusting the origin covers all paths and query strings on that host, so ownership and intended use of the endpoint should be confirmed before merging.
- This changes only link-protection behavior. It does not automatically authenticate the user, grant consent, alter workspace trust, or bypass browser protections.

## Acceptance criteria

- `https://logic-apis-centralus.consent.azure-apim.net` is included in `linkProtectionTrustedDomains` for Stable, Insiders, and Exploration product configurations.
- Links to the HTTPS origin open without the VS Code external-website confirmation.
- Other `azure-apim.net` hosts remain untrusted and continue to show link protection.
- Product JSON validation passes.
"}

## Description

The "Open in Agents Window" button expands on hover, shifting the title bar layout and making it easy to activate accidentally.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Move the pointer just to the right of the "Open in Agents Window" button.
1. The button expands, shifting the title bar layout.
1. Click the area where the button was before the layout shifted.
1. "Open in Agents Window" is activated unintentionally.

## Expected Behavior

The title bar layout should remain stable on hover to prevent accidental activation of adjacent controls.

## Additional Context

The setting `"chat.titleBar.openInAgentsWindow.enabled": false` disables the button as a workaround."}

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

## Description

The "Open in Agents Window" button expands on hover, shifting the title bar layout and making it easy to activate accidentally.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Move the pointer just to the right of the "Open in Agents Window" button.
1. The button expands, shifting the title bar layout.
1. Click the area where the button was before the layout shifted.
1. "Open in Agents Window" is activated unintentionally.

## Expected Behavior

The title bar layout should remain stable on hover to prevent accidental activation of adjacent controls.

## Additional Context

The setting `"chat.titleBar.openInAgentsWindow.enabled": false` disables the button as a workaround."}

{"body":" Type: Bug ### Summary When the built-in AI features are enabled (`chat.disableAIFeatures: false`), a `Code Helper` process (agent-host) immediately starts using ~180–200% CPU and its memory footprint grows continuously without ever stabilizing. Setting `chat.disableAIFeatures: true` stops the growth instantly; re-enabling it brings the problem back right away. The GitHub Copilot / Copilot Chat extensions are **not** installed — this comes from the AI features built into VS Code itself. ### Observed behavior - `Code Helper` (agent-host) jumps from ~0% to ~180% CPU within seconds of enabling AI features (see attached screenshot, PID 33728: 180.9% CPU, memory already climbing). - Memory footprint grows linearly, roughly **4 GB → 7 GB in about one hour**, with no plateau. - CPU stays at ~190–200% the whole time, even while the editor is idle. - CPU die temperature reaches 97–104 °C. - A separate `copilot-runtime` process is also running, but stays low (~2% CPU, ~60 MB). **1. Right after enabling AI features:** CPU jumps to ~180% immediately. **2. After ~30 minutes with AI features enabled:** memory footprint keeps growing linearly. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open any folder/workspace on macOS (Apple Silicon). 2. Make sure `chat.disableAIFeatures` is `false`. 3. Open a file and start editing normally. 4. Watch the `Code Helper` process in Activity Monitor: CPU goes to ~180% and memory keeps growing. 5. Set `chat.disableAIFeatures` to `true` → growth stops immediately. ### What I already tried - Updated VS Code to the latest version — still reproducible. - Reproduced in different projects, from a small one (~150 files) to a large one, so it doesn't seem related to workspace size. - Added a large vendor framework folder to `files.watcherExclude` — no change. - Ruled out my other extensions (GitLens, Git Graph, ES7+ React snippets, Claude Code for VS Code); the issue follows only the `chat.disableAIFeatures` setting. ### Expected behavior The agent-host process should settle to low CPU usage when idle and keep a bounded memory footprint. ### Workaround I currently toggle `chat.disableAIFeatures` on and off with a keybinding, enabling AI features only when I need inline suggestions, and reload the window when memory gets too high. request.text:
{"body":"### Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?
Not applicable: the code is in the built-in Copilot Chat extension.

- VS Code: 1.143.0
- Copilot Chat: 0.71.0
- OS: Windows 11

### Steps to reproduce

1. Get any chat reply containing a file link with a line range, the form the extension's own `<fileLinkification>` instructions ask models to use, e.g. `[a.py](a.py#L5-L7)`.
2. Click the link.

**Expected:** lines 5 through 7 are selected.
**Actual:** the selection runs from line 5, column 1 to line 7, column 1. Line 7 is not selected. The range's last line is always left out, so a link to a single function's closing line (or a one-line range like `#L5-L6`) shows less than the model meant.

This is independent of the model: it reproduces with any model whose reply contains the link.

### Cause

`parseAnchor` in `extensions/copilot/src/extension/linkify/common/modelFilePathLinkifier.ts` builds the range with column 0 at both ends, so the end position is the start of the last line:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f303fd73d506a3fc1c1db9b2068d1127c9cfff23/extensions/copilot/src/extension/linkify/common/modelFilePathLinkifier.ts#L233

```ts
range: new Range(new Position(start, 0), new Position(end, 0)),
```

The stored chat references confirm it: a `#L549-L560` link is saved as `startLineNumber: 549, startColumn: 1, endLineNumber: 560, endColumn: 1`.

### Suggested fix

End the range at the end of the last line, e.g. `new Position(end + 1, 0)` or `new Position(end, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)` (validated against the document), so the inclusive line range the anchor names is selected in full.
"}

{"body":"In the Chat Customizations editor, opening an item from a section list (e.g. Instructions > User) and then going back always returns the list scrolled to the top, losing your place.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Add enough user instructions that the Instructions > User list scrolls (e.g. 20).
2. Scroll partway down the list.
3. Click an item to open its detail view.
4. Click back.

**Expected:** the list is at the scroll position it had before opening the item.
**Actual:** the list is scrolled to the top.

**Cause:** while the list is hidden (`display: none`), its resize observer still triggers a section layout. `layoutVirtualizedSections` measures a zero-height root and falls back to each section's full content height, so the list is laid out at its content height and `scrollTop` is clamped to 0 before it can be restored.

This affects every list using `layoutVirtualizedSectionList` (prompt sections, plugins, tools, migration); the MCP list already skips layout while hidden.

I have a fix with a unit test in #337705."}

{"body":" Type: Bug In a multi-root workspace, one folder from an extension file system (SAP ADT, scheme `abap:`) breaks custom agent and skill discovery for all folders in Copilot harness sessions. The Local harness works. **Steps** 1. Open a local folder with `.github/agents/*.agent.md` and `.github/skills/*/SKILL.md`. 2. Add an ABAP package folder with **ABAP: Add Package as Folder to Workspace...** (SAP ADT extension). 3. Start a Copilot harness chat and open the agent picker. **Actual:** the workspace agents and skills are missing. `agenthost.log`: ``` [SessionCustomizationDiscovery] Error during discovery: Request agents.discover failed with message: Invalid working directory, projectPaths: /Users//, /repotree-v1/, /repotree-v1//System Library/ ``` The `abap:` scheme is stripped, and the invalid path fails the whole list. {"body":"@roblourens as discussed with @bryanchen-d, this is agreed to be worth solving later, so it's filed for tracking rather than for immediate action.

## Summary

The VS Code desktop client bundles two different Copilot native runtimes:
- the core Agent Host's runtime from `@github/copilot-sdk`
- the built-in Copilot extension's own runtime from `@github/copilot`

On macOS arm64 they make up **26% of the client zip**. Every macOS user downloads both. Because ESRP signing and notarization time grows with payload size, they also add about 2 minutes to every official build's time to ship.

The question for the owners: **when the Copilot extension ships built in, can it use the core runtime instead of bundling its own?**

## What ships today

Measured on official insider build [486716](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=486716), artifact `vscode_client_darwin_arm64_archive` (319 MB zip, 917 MB uncompressed).

| Runtime | Package and version | Path in the app | Raw | Compressed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Core (Agent Host) | `@github/copilot-sdk-darwin-arm64` 1.0.23-preview.5 (`copilotRuntimeVersion` 1.0.100-1 in root `package.json`) | `Resources/app/node_modules.asar.unpacked/@github/copilot-sdk-darwin-arm64/prebuilds/darwin-arm64/runtime.node` | 101 MB | 48 MB |
| Copilot extension | `@github/copilot` 1.0.73 (`"^1.0.73"` in `extensions/copilot/package.json`) | `Resources/app/extensions/copilot/node_modules/@github/copilot/sdk/prebuilds/darwin-arm64/runtime.node` | 83 MB | 34 MB |

- They are different builds, not byte duplicates (different SHA-256 and versions). Deduplicating files at build time can't remove either one.
- Together they are **82 MB of the 319 MB zip (26%)**. For comparison, Electron Framework is 120 MB.
- **Universal carries both arches of each runtime.** The universal client zip is 546 MB and the universal DMG is 490 MB, versus 319 MB and 286 MB for arm64.
- The other macOS packages are affected by the same choice: the per-arch DMGs, and x64 at roughly the same proportions (client zip 341 MB).

## Why the extension carries its own runtime

These are observations from the source, for the owners to confirm or correct.

- `extensions/copilot` uses `@github/copilot/sdk` for its Copilot CLI chat sessions (`src/extension/chatSessions/copilotcli/node/copilotCli.ts` dynamically imports `@github/copilot/sdk`).
- The extension also ships separately (Marketplace/VSIX), so in that form it has to bring its own runtime.
- The core Agent Host uses `@github/copilot-sdk` and pins a separate runtime version (`copilotRuntimeVersion` 1.0.100-1), so the two runtimes move on independent version tracks.
- There is already a precedent for sharing natives when the extension is built in. `extensions/copilot/src/extension/chatSessions/copilotcli/AGENTS.md` says the bundled path resolves node-pty from VS Code's own app tree, and build-time packaging (`build/lib/copilot.ts`) materializes only the ripgrep shim. The runtime itself is not shared today.

## Questions for the owners

1. Does the built-in extension need its own runtime version, for example because of an API contract between `@github/copilot` 1.0.73 and the core runtime 1.0.100? Or could it load the core runtime when running built in, the same way it already reuses node-pty?
2. If the versions must differ, could the built-in extension skip its runtime and fall back to the Marketplace path only when versions are incompatible?
3. Is one runtime in the built-in product the end state, either way?

## Expected effect if the built-in extension reuses the core runtime

| | Today | Without the extension's runtime | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| arm64 client zip | 319 MB | ~285 MB | −34 MB (−11%) per download |
| x64 client zip | 341 MB | ~305 MB | about −35 MB |
| Universal client zip | 546 MB | ~480 MB | about −65 MB (both arches) |
| x64/arm64 client sign + notarize (critical path inside Sign) | sign 9.6–10.5 min, notarize 16.2–18.1 min | | about −2 min |
| Universal sign + notarize | 12.7 + 22.0 min | | about −4 min |
| Official build time to ship (median 88 min) | | | about −2 min on average |

How the build-time numbers were derived:
- **Size vs duration:** across 190 ESRP operations from 30 macOS Sign jobs since Oct 15, duration correlates with payload size (r = 0.71 for sign, 0.78 for notarize), at about 1.9 min per 100 MB of ESRP-reported payload.
- **Which job is the bottleneck:** the client zip is the slowest codesign and the slowest notarization in 34 of 40 Sign jobs.
- **Which jobs set ship time:** macOS X64 Sign or Universal Sign is the last product job in 23 of 34 green, no-retry official builds since Oct 8.
- **Not measured:** Windows and Linux packages very likely carry both runtimes too. That would cost them download size, but not ship time, since they aren't on the critical path.

## Not in scope

- No pipeline change is proposed. Packaging should follow whatever the owners decide.
- The Mermaid extension also ships the same chunks twice (`notebook-out` and `markdown-preview-out`, about 5 MB compressed). That is worth a separate small cleanup, but it has no measurable build-time effect.

> Co-authored with Copilot
"}

{"body":"### Describe the problem

Nixpkgs does not say which English spelling to use in its documentation, and the manuals currently mix several.  Authors and reviewers have no rule to follow.

I could not find a rule in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `doc/README.md`, `doc/styleguide.md` (added in #523597) or the NixOS manual's contributing chapter.  The Nix manual does have one: ["Use British English"](https://github.com/NixOS/nix/blob/master/doc/manual/source/development/documentation.md), described as "a somewhat arbitrary choice to force consistency" (NixOS/nix#9017).  It does not say whether to write `-ise` or `-ize`, and the manual's own text is mixed (last row of the table below).

Three spelling standards are in play:

- American spelling: `color`, `center`, `defense`, `catalog`, `organize`, `analyze`.
- [Oxford spelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_spelling), British spelling with `-ize` and `-yse` as used by Oxford University Press and many international bodies: `colour`, `centre`, `defence`, `catalogue`, `organize`, `analyse`.
- British spelling with `-ise`, as in `nix-store --realise` and `nix store optimise`: `colour`, `centre`, `defence`, `catalogue`, `organise`, `analyse`.

Rough whole-word counts for Nixpkgs at dd7f9cacc519 and the Nix manual at NixOS/nix@42d96171bbef.  The first two columns count ten word pairs (behaviour/behavior, favour/favor, artefact/artifact, catalogue/catalog, defence/defense, labelled/labeled, modelling/modeling, cancelled/canceled, analyse/analyze, neighbour/neighbor), where British and Oxford spelling agree against American.  The last two columns count `-ise` against `-ize` forms of about 50 verb stems (initialise, optimise, customise and so on), where Oxford spelling sides with American.

| Where | British and Oxford (`behaviour`) | American (`behavior`) | `-ise` | `-ize` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

{"body":"<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not verified. Disabling Agent Plugins and a custom Markdown preview extension did not prevent recurrence; this was not an all-extensions-disabled test.

- VS Code Version: 1.143.0 (Stable, user setup)
- Commit: `2d0b7506a36c1d6db9a466440131a8e01eab2289`
- OS Version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26100
- Electron: 43.7.7
- Chromium: 150.0.7871.250
- Node.js: 24.21.0
- V8: 15.0.245.31-electron.0
- Bundled Copilot: `@github/copilot 1.0.100-1`, `@github/copilot-sdk 1.0.23-preview.5`
- Remote environment: Linux over SSH [distribution/version not yet collected]
- Feature: Copilot in the separate Agents window
- Copilot Chat and Remote-SSH extension versions: Not yet collected

## Summary

The separate Agents window's memory usage grows over time toward 4 GB and eventually crashes with an out-of-memory error. In VS Code's Process Explorer, the affected entry is `window [4] (Agents)`.

This still happens when starting a new Agent session with both of these settings disabled:

```json
{
  "chat.plugins.enabled": false,
  "chat.agentHost.ahpJsonlLoggingEnabled": false
}
```

Memory sometimes drops as it approaches 4 GB, then grows again after a short time. Those drops did not prevent a subsequent OOM crash.

## Observed workflow

These are the conditions in the affected environment, not a minimal standalone reproducer:

1. Use a Copilot session in the separate Agents window.
2. Start a new session with the two settings above disabled.
3. Monitor `window [4] (Agents)` in VS Code's Process Explorer over time.
4. Observe memory growing toward 4 GB, dropping temporarily, then growing again.
5. Eventually the window terminates with:

```text
The window terminated unexpectedly (reason: 'oom', code: '-536870904')
```

Earlier occurrences happened both while the agent was working and while the session was idle.

Expected: The Agents window remains usable without exhausting memory during a session.

Actual: The window crashes with OOM, interrupting use of the agent.

## Additional observations

- Earlier `main.log` entries also recorded:
  ```text
  CodeWindow: renderer process gone (reason: oom, code: -536870904)
  ```
- A custom Mermaid/Markdown preview extension was disabled and VS Code was reloaded during troubleshooting. OOM subsequently recurred, so that change alone did not resolve the issue.
- Starting a new session did not stop the memory growth.
- A crash dump was captured but is not attached because it may contain private memory contents.

## Investigation limits

The precise trigger and retained objects have not been isolated. No all-extensions-disabled, clean-profile, minimal-repository, or confirmed latest-Insiders comparison result is available. Process Explorer's reported memory alone does not establish the JavaScript heap size or a particular leak mechanism.

The visible failure is the Agents window renderer; this report does not establish a remote Agent Host OOM.

## Potentially related reports

- #343006 describes an Agents renderer OOM caused by large shell output. I have not established that trigger or code path in this case.
- #334892 describes a plugin-sync/Base64 renderer OOM. This case still occurred with `chat.plugins.enabled: false`.
- #339918 describes excessive worktree scanning and AHP logging in the Agents renderer. It is marked fixed in Insiders, but I have not verified whether this build includes that fix or whether this case has the same cause.

I am reporting these observations separately because the matching root cause has not been established.

"}
